title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄序
賢才致治之本也自昔御天
下者必資之以共理焉周子
曰心純則賢才輔賢才輔則
天下治治於乎人君未嘗不願
治也而必藉賢才之輔賢才
未嘗不輔世也而必自君心
===
之純君心既純于以用天下
之賢才于以大一統之鴻業
于以開萬世之太平卓乎不
可尚已山東密邇京畿凡百
供億倍蓰僕服歲屬庚子適
當鄉試之期所司舉行舊典
時巡按監察御史張蕙仰體
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄序

賢才，致治之本也。自昔御天下者，必資之以共理焉。周子曰：「心純則賢才輔，賢才輔則天下治治。」於乎！人君未嘗不願治也，而必藉賢才之輔；賢才未嘗不輔世也，而必自君心之純。君心既純，于以用天下之賢才，于以大一統之鴻業，于以開萬世之太平，卓乎不可尚已。

山東密邇京畿，凡百供億，倍蓰僕服。歲屬庚子，適當鄉試之期，所司舉行舊典。時巡按監察御史張蕙仰體
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

Worthy and talented men are the foundation of good government. Since ancient times, those who ruled all under Heaven have necessarily relied upon them to share in governing. Master Zhou said: “When the heart is pure, worthy and talented men lend their assistance; when worthy and talented men lend their assistance, all under Heaven is well governed.” [The transcription repeats “governed” (治).] Alas! Rulers have always desired good government, yet they must rely upon the assistance of worthy and talented men. Worthy and talented men have always assisted the world, yet this must originate in the purity of the ruler’s heart. Once the ruler’s heart is pure, he can employ the worthy and talented men of the realm, enlarge the magnificent undertaking of universal unity, and inaugurate peace for ten thousand generations. Such excellence cannot be surpassed.

Shandong lies close to the capital region; its manifold obligations to furnish supplies and perform service are several times greater [?]. The year was gengzi [1480], and the time for the Provincial Examination had duly arrived. The responsible officials carried out the established procedures. At that time, Zhang Hui, the Regional Inspector, respectfully took to heart…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
朝廷簡賢圖治之盛心迺迺協謀
於藩臬重臣以為命鄉論秀
事莫重於此者有所容心焉
是負
國也是怠厥官也毋私毋怠惟
公與慎此今日之急務舍是
他圖惡在其為知所重耶因
===
儀提學僉事畢瑜預考應試
之士千七百有奇偕參政裴
慧孫曄參議王道僉事劉瑋
葉淇羅睿侯恂表端相與申
嚴小試以杜倖進而至公之
道如青天白日於是取其通
經學古可以備場屋之選者
punctuated: 朝廷簡賢圖治之盛心，迺迺協謀於藩臬重臣，以為命鄉論秀，事莫重於此者。有所容心焉，是負國也，是怠厥官也。毋私毋怠，惟公與慎，此今日之急務。舍是他圖，惡在其為知所重耶？因儀提學僉事畢瑜預考應試之士千七百有奇，偕參政裴慧、孫曄，參議王道，僉事劉瑋、葉淇、羅睿、侯恂、表端，相與申嚴小試，以杜倖進，而至公之道如青天白日。於是取其通經學古、可以備場屋之選者，
translation_en:
…the court’s lofty aspiration to select worthy men and achieve good government. He then [?] consulted with the senior officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, holding that nothing was more important than directing the local selection and appraisal of outstanding scholars. To allow personal motives any place in this would be to fail the state and neglect one’s official duties. Neither partiality nor negligence was permissible: impartiality and care were the urgent duties of the day. If one abandoned these to pursue other aims, how could one claim to know what mattered most?

Thereupon [?], Bi Yu, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner overseeing education, conducted a preliminary examination of more than seventeen hundred candidates. Together with Vice Administration Commissioners Pei Hui and Sun Ye, Assistant Administration Commissioner Wang Dao, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Liu Wei, Ye Qi, Luo Rui, Hou Xun, and Biao Duan [?], he reinforced the rigor of the preliminary tests to prevent advancement through mere good fortune. Their complete impartiality was as manifest as the blue sky and bright sun. They then selected those who understood the classics and studied antiquity, and who could qualify as candidates for the examination…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
僅七百五十餘人綱維防範
則巡按御史寶監臨之提調
則左布政使趙文博左參政
邢表監試則副使李讓石渠
雖下至受卷彌封諸執事亦
必慎柬諸有司之廉慎者充
焉凡厥三試天日晴明祥飇
===
披拂諸士子揚眉吐氣有激
昂青雲之志比撤棘得其文
詞之純如渭之純於清如玉
之純於白如黃鍾大呂之純
於和者七十五人遵
制額也寔精選也事竣告成於
上而傳示於下昭乘司文衡宜序
punctuated: 僅七百五十餘人。綱維防範，則巡按御史寶監臨之；提調，則左布政使趙文博、左參政邢表；監試，則副使李讓、石渠。雖下至受卷、彌封諸執事，亦必慎柬諸有司之廉慎者充焉。凡厥三試，天日晴明，祥飇披拂，諸士子揚眉吐氣，有激昂青雲之志。比撤棘，得其文詞之純，如渭之純於清，如玉之純於白，如黃鍾大呂之純於和者七十五人。遵制額也，寔精選也。事竣，告成於上，而傳示於下。昭乘司文衡，宜序
translation_en:
…only a little over seven hundred and fifty men. For oversight and safeguards, the Regional Inspector Bao served as Supervising Official. The Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhao Wenbo and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Xing Biao; the examination monitors were Surveillance Vice Commissioners Li Rang and Shi Qu. Even the staff responsible for receiving papers, sealing candidates’ names, and other duties had to be carefully selected from honest and conscientious officials.

Throughout all three examination sessions, the skies were clear and bright, and an auspicious breeze brushed gently over the candidates. They lifted their brows and breathed freely, their spirits stirred by aspirations to rise to the clouds. By the time the thorn enclosure was dismantled, seventy-five men had been selected whose writing was pure—as the Wei River is pure in its clarity, as jade is pure in its whiteness, and as the Huangzhong and Dalu pitch standards are pure in their harmony. This complied with the imperially prescribed quota; it was indeed a selection of the finest. Once the work was finished, its completion was reported to the throne and the results circulated to those below. Zhaocheng [?], charged with weighing literary merit, ought to write a preface…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
諸首切惟人以耶然之身可
以參天地可以贊元化可以
奠安宗社可以康乂生民斯
文倚之為命脉衣冠賴之以
維持何莫不自一心始耶二
帝純此心以帝天下三王純
此心以王天下孔孟純此心
===
以師天下厥後聖學失傳
心始雜于刑名下貴老□□
于夷君子叡論也至於有宋
五星聚奎濂洛關閩諸君子
出闡明心學以續寥寥墜緒不
能追復帝王之治於當時猶
得以淑人心維世道之綱厥功
punctuated: 諸首。切惟人以耶然之身，可以參天地，可以贊元化，可以奠安宗社，可以康乂生民。斯文倚之為命脉，衣冠賴之以維持，何莫不自一心始耶？二帝純此心以帝天下，三王純此心以王天下，孔孟純此心以師天下。厥後聖學失傳，心始雜于刑名，下貴老□□于夷，君子叡論也。至於有宋，五星聚奎，濂洛關閩諸君子出，闡明心學，以續寥寥墜緒。不能追復帝王之治於當時，猶得以淑人心，維世道之綱。厥功
translation_en: …at its beginning. I earnestly reflect that human beings, with their bodies described here as “yeran” [?], can stand alongside Heaven and Earth, assist the primordial work of transformation, secure the ancestral temples and altars of state, and bring peace and good government to the people. This cultural tradition depends upon them for its lifeblood, and the community of the learned relies upon them for its preservation. Does not all this begin with the single mind? The Two Emperors purified this mind and thereby ruled All-under-Heaven as emperors; the Three Kings purified this mind and thereby ruled All-under-Heaven as kings; Confucius and Mencius purified this mind and thereby became teachers to All-under-Heaven. Thereafter, the transmission of the learning of the sages was lost, and the mind began to be mixed with the doctrines of punishments and names. The following passage appears to mention esteeming Lao, the Yi, and the wise discussions of gentlemen, but is garbled and includes two illegible characters [?]. When the Song dynasty arose, the five planets gathered in the constellation Kui. The gentlemen of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min emerged and elucidated the learning of the mind, continuing its tenuous, interrupted transmission. Although they could not restore the government of the ancient emperors and kings in their own time, they nevertheless succeeded in improving people's minds and sustaining the guiding principles of the moral order. Their achievement…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
偉矣蓋人之心純則誠否則
僞純則正否則邪純則公否
則私純則善否則惡純則君
子否則小人出乎此則入乎
彼甚可畏也爾多士養於庠
序以純其心發於文章以純
乎理英英乎氣之充也彬彬
===
乎才之碩也亹亹乎論議之
正大也登名是錄亦榮矣行
將角藝春官對揚
大廷際雲龍風虎之嘉會有日
繼自今定心制行其必純乎
誠而無僞純乎正而無邪純
乎公而無私純乎善而無惡
punctuated: 偉矣！蓋人之心，純則誠，否則僞；純則正，否則邪；純則公，否則私；純則善，否則惡；純則君子，否則小人。出乎此，則入乎彼，甚可畏也。爾多士養於庠序，以純其心；發於文章，以純乎理。英英乎氣之充也，彬彬乎才之碩也，亹亹乎論議之正大也！登名是錄，亦榮矣。行將角藝春官，對揚大廷，際雲龍風虎之嘉會有日。繼自今，定心制行，其必純乎誠而無僞，純乎正而無邪，純乎公而無私，純乎善而無惡，
translation_en:
…was great indeed! When a person’s heart is pure, it is sincere; otherwise, it is false. When pure, it is upright; otherwise, depraved. When pure, it is public-spirited; otherwise, selfish. When pure, it is good; otherwise, evil. With purity one is a gentleman; otherwise, a petty man. To depart from the one is to enter the other: this is greatly to be feared.

You many scholars have been nurtured in the schools to purify your hearts, and have expressed yourselves in literary compositions in pure accord with principle. How splendid the fullness of your vital spirit! How refined your ample talents! How unflagging your upright and broad-minded discussions! To have your names entered in this record is indeed an honor. Soon you will compete in literary skill at the Ministry of Rites and respond to the sovereign in the great imperial court. The day will come when you enjoy an auspicious meeting of ruler and worthy ministers, as clouds follow the dragon and winds the tiger. From this time onward, steady your hearts and regulate your conduct. Be sure to remain purely sincere, without falsity; purely upright, without depravity; purely public-spirited, without selfishness; purely good, without evil…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
純乎君子而不為小人之歸
緌成化理上侔帝王之盛使
天下後世稱之曰齊魯人才
功名德業遠可以趾美孔孟
高可以仰止泰岱豈惟爾多
士之光而昭等亦與有光於
無窮也因序茲錄庸丕汝多
===
士於成
江西廣信府儒學教授福清
鄭昭謹序
punctuated:
純乎君子而不為小人之歸，緌成化理，上侔帝王之盛，使天下後世稱之曰：「齊魯人才，功名德業，遠可以趾美孔孟，高可以仰止泰岱。」豈惟爾多士之光，而昭等亦與有光於無窮也。因序茲錄，庸丕汝多士於成。
江西廣信府儒學教授福清鄭昭謹序。
translation_en:
…be purely gentlemen and never end as petty men; bring transformation and good government to fruition [?], matching the flourishing rule of the ancient emperors and kings, so that all under Heaven and later generations will praise you, saying: “The talented men of Qi and Lu, in their achievements, distinction, virtue, and accomplishments, can follow the distant example of Kongzi and Mengzi and rival their excellence; in their loftiness, they can be looked up to like Mount Tai.” Would this bring glory only to you assembled scholars? I, Zheng Zhao, and my colleagues would also share in that glory forever. I therefore write this preface to the record, thereby encouraging you assembled scholars toward accomplishment [?].
Preface respectfully composed by Zheng Zhao of Fuqing, Instructor in the Confucian School of Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
恭則不侮寬則得衆信則人任焉敏則有
功惠則足以使人
故君子之道本諸身徵諸庶民考諸三王
而不謬建諸天地而不悖質諸鬼神而
無疑百世以俟聖人而不惑
我非堯舜之道不敢以陳於王前故齊人
莫如我敬王也
===
易
觀乎人文以化成天下
九二鳴鶴在陰其子和之我有好爵吾與
爾靡之象曰其子和之中心願也
富有之謂大業日新之謂盛德
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
與剛立人之道曰仁與義兼三才而兩
之故易六畫而成卦分陰分陽迭用柔
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

恭則不侮，寬則得衆，信則人任焉，敏則有功，惠則足以使人。

故君子之道，本諸身，徵諸庶民，考諸三王而不謬，建諸天地而不悖，質諸鬼神而無疑，百世以俟聖人而不惑。

我非堯舜之道，不敢以陳於王前，故齊人莫如我敬王也。

易

觀乎人文，以化成天下。

九二：鳴鶴在陰，其子和之；我有好爵，吾與爾靡之。象曰：「其子和之」，中心願也。

富有之謂大業，日新之謂盛德。

昔者聖人之作易也，將以順性命之理，是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

If you are respectful, you will not be insulted; if you are generous, you will win the multitude; if you are trustworthy, others will entrust you with responsibilities; if you are diligent, you will achieve results; if you are beneficent, you will be able to employ others in your service.

Thus the gentleman’s Way is rooted in his own person and verified among the common people. Tested against the Three Kings, it is without error; established before Heaven and Earth, it does not conflict with them; submitted to the spirits, it leaves no doubt; and even if he awaits a sage a hundred generations hence, he will have no misgivings.

Unless it accords with the Way of Yao and Shun, I dare not present it before the king. Thus no one in Qi respects the king as I do.

Book of Changes

Observe human culture in order to transform and perfect all under Heaven.

Nine in the second place: A crane calls in the shade, and its young answers it. I have a fine cup of wine; I will share it with you. The Image Commentary says: “Its young answers it”—this is what it desires in its inmost heart.

Abundant possession is called a great undertaking; daily renewal is called flourishing virtue.

In ancient times, when the sages made the Book of Changes, they intended to follow the principles of human nature and destiny. Thus they established the Way of Heaven as yin and yang, the Way of Earth as yielding and firm, and the Way of humanity as benevolence and righteousness. They encompassed the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and doubled each; thus in the Changes six lines form a hexagram. Distinguishing yin and yang, they employed alternately the yielding…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
剛故易六位而成章
書
誰敢不讓敢不敬應
從諫弗咈先民時若居上克明爲下克忠
與人不求備檢身若不及
其克詰爾戎兵以陟禹之迹方行天下至
于海表罔有不服以覲文王之耿光以
揚武王之大烈
昔君文武丕平富不務咎底至齊信用昭
===
明于天下則亦有熊羆之士不二心之
臣保乂王家用端命于上帝皇天用訓
厥道付畀四方
詩
淑人君子其儀不忒其儀不忒正是四國
俾爾單厚何福不除
亹亹申伯王纘之事于邑于謝南國是式
王釐爾成來咨來茹嗟嗟保介維莫之春
亦又何求如何新畬於皇來牟將受厥
punctuated:
剛，故易六位而成章。

書
誰敢不讓，敢不敬應？
從諫弗咈，先民時若。居上克明，爲下克忠。與人不求備，檢身若不及。
其克詰爾戎兵，以陟禹之迹，方行天下，至于海表，罔有不服，以覲文王之耿光，以揚武王之大烈。
昔君文武，丕平富，不務咎，底至齊信，用昭明于天下。則亦有熊羆之士、不二心之臣，保乂王家，用端命于上帝。皇天用訓厥道，付畀四方。

詩
淑人君子，其儀不忒。其儀不忒，正是四國。
俾爾單厚，何福不除？
亹亹申伯，王纘之事。于邑于謝，南國是式。
王釐爾成，來咨來茹。
嗟嗟保介，維莫之春，亦又何求？如何新畬？於皇來牟，將受厥
translation_en:
…the firm; thus the six positions of the Changes form a complete pattern.

Book of Documents
Who would dare not yield, or dare not respond respectfully?
Follow remonstrance without resisting it, and take the men of old as your models. In a superior position, be discerning; in a subordinate position, be loyal. Do not demand perfection of others; examine yourself as though you still fell short.
Put your weapons and troops in good order, and advance over the lands where Yu left his traces. Proceed unhindered throughout the realm, even beyond the seas, so that none fail to submit, thereby displaying King Wen’s brilliant glory and exalting King Wu’s great achievements.
The former rulers, Wen and Wu, brought great peace and prosperity. They did not devote themselves to finding fault, but attained perfect impartiality and trustworthiness [?], thereby shining throughout the realm. They also had warriors like bears and loyal ministers of undivided allegiance, who protected and governed the royal house, thereby securing its mandate from the Lord on High. August Heaven accordingly approved their way and entrusted the four quarters to them.

Book of Odes
That virtuous man, that noble gentleman—his deportment is without fault. His deportment is without fault, and he sets the states of the four quarters aright.
May you be abundantly blessed: what blessing would not be bestowed upon you?
Diligent is the Earl of Shen; the king entrusted him with continuing the work. He established his city at Xie, serving as a model for the southern states.
The king has granted you success; come, deliberate and consider.

楚子、陳侯、鄭伯盟于辰陵。〔宣公十一年〕公及楚人、秦人、宋人、陳人、衛人、鄭人、齊人、曹人、邾人、薛人、鄫人盟于蜀。〔成公二年〕叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚屈建、蔡公孫歸生、衛石惡、陳孔奐、鄭良霄、許人、曹人于宋。〔襄公二十七年〕叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚公子圍、齊國弱、宋向戌、衛齊惡、陳公子招、蔡公孫歸生、鄭罕虎、許人、曹人于虢。〔昭公元年〕
禮記
太傅在前，少傅在後，入則有保，出則有師，是以教喻而德成也。
義生然後禮作，禮作然後萬物安。
故聽其雅頌之聲，志意得廣焉。

translation_en:
…and only after the toasting are cups offered to the servicemen. The servicemen raise their cups, and toasts circulate in turn; only after the toasting are cups offered to the younger sons. The sacrificial stands and vessels, portions of sacrificial animals, and offerings of food all have graded distinctions, thereby making clear the distinction between noble and humble.

Second Session
Discourse
For the ruler and his chief ministers, acting as father and mother to all under Heaven constitutes the Kingly Way.

Edict, proclamation, and memorial 〔One topic from among these [?]〕

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
問聖人之心見於書猶化工之妙著於物
聖人之書行於世猶日月之運麗乎天
粤自馬圖見而羲卦畫龜書呈而禹疇
敘文王因羲畫而繫繇辭武王訪箕子
而衍洪範是數聖人之書皆所以為天
地立心為生民立命為萬世開太平者
也後世英君誼辟工於辭章者若大風
鴻鵠諸歌勤於著述者若金鑑帝範等
書果可以比擬前數聖人之書歟洪惟
===
我
朝
太祖高皇帝御製大誥三編
太宗文皇帝御製為善陰隲孝順事實二書
宣宗章皇帝御製五倫書皆垂世之寶訓也
列聖之心即古聖人之心
列聖之書即古聖人之書然三誥兼紀善惡二
書專載善孝五倫書備著五倫之道日
兼紀善惡以示勸懲者以孰為最紀善
punctuated: 問：聖人之心見於書，猶化工之妙著於物；聖人之書行於世，猶日月之運麗乎天。粤自馬圖見而羲卦畫，龜書呈而禹疇敘，文王因羲畫而繫繇辭，武王訪箕子而衍洪範，是數聖人之書，皆所以為天地立心、為生民立命、為萬世開太平者也。後世英君誼辟，工於辭章者若大風、鴻鵠諸歌，勤於著述者若金鑑、帝範等書，果可以比擬前數聖人之書歟？洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝御製《大誥》三編，太宗文皇帝御製《為善陰隲》《孝順事實》二書，宣宗章皇帝御製《五倫書》，皆垂世之寶訓也。列聖之心，即古聖人之心；列聖之書，即古聖人之書。然三誥兼紀善惡，二書專載善孝，《五倫書》備著五倫之道。日：兼紀善惡以示勸懲者，以孰為最？紀善
translation_en:
Question: The minds of the sages are revealed in their writings, just as the wondrous workings of creation are manifested in things. The writings of the sages circulate in the world, just as the sun and moon move across the heavens. From the time when the horse diagram appeared and Fuxi drew the trigrams, and when the tortoise writing was presented and Yu set out the categories, King Wen appended divinatory statements to Fuxi’s figures, and King Wu consulted Jizi and elaborated the Great Plan. The writings of these sages all served to establish a mind for Heaven and Earth, to establish a destiny for the people, and to inaugurate enduring peace for all generations. Among the brilliant sovereigns and righteous rulers of later ages, those skilled in literary composition produced such songs as Great Wind and Wild Swans, while those devoted to authorship produced such books as Golden Mirror and Model for Emperors. Can these truly be compared with the writings of the aforementioned sages?
We reverently consider the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements, imperially composed by our dynasty’s Emperor Taizu Gao; the two books, Hidden Recompense for Doing Good and Accounts of Filial Obedience, imperially composed by Emperor Taizong Wen; and the Book of the Five Relationships, imperially composed by Emperor Xuanzong Zhang. All are precious teachings handed down to posterity. The minds of our successive sage emperors are the minds of the ancient sages; their writings are the writings of the ancient sages. Yet the three Pronouncements record both good and evil, the two books exclusively recount goodness and filial conduct, and the Book of the Five Relationships fully sets forth the Way of the five relationships. The question is [?]: among the accounts recording both good and evil to encourage and admonish, which is foremost? Among those recording goodness…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
孝以示勸者以孰爲優盡五倫者孰可
爲法歟明著于篇毋隱
問學莫先於窮理如心性誠敬皆理之所
當窮者姑相與論之自大舜開萬世心
學之源而後之言心者祖焉成湯發萬
世性學之蘊而後之言性者祖焉心一
也何以有人心道心心爲太極心妙性
情之異歟性一也何以有天命氣質善
惡三品之分歟六經言誠者有矣言敬
===
者有矣自漢以來無人識誠字先儒有
以不欺言者有以不息言者有以無妄
言者何說始盡歟自秦以來無人識敬
字先儒有以整齊嚴肅言者有以常惺
惺法言者有以其心收斂不容一物言
者何說始備歟夫心也性也誠也敬也
果可一以貫之歟諸士子講學有年幸
紬繹以對
問六經之後而詩文衆體出焉不可以不
punctuated:
孝以示勸者，以孰爲優？盡五倫者，孰可爲法歟？明著于篇，毋隱。

問：學莫先於窮理，如心性誠敬，皆理之所當窮者，姑相與論之。自大舜開萬世心學之源，而後之言心者祖焉；成湯發萬世性學之蘊，而後之言性者祖焉。心一也，何以有人心、道心、心爲太極、心妙性情之異歟？性一也，何以有天命、氣質、善惡、三品之分歟？六經言誠者有矣，言敬者有矣。自漢以來，無人識誠字。先儒有以不欺言者，有以不息言者，有以無妄言者，何說始盡歟？自秦以來，無人識敬字。先儒有以整齊嚴肅言者，有以常惺惺法言者，有以其心收斂不容一物言者，何說始備歟？夫心也，性也，誠也，敬也，果可一以貫之歟？諸士子講學有年，幸紬繹以對。

問：六經之後，而詩文衆體出焉，不可以不
translation_en:
…filial piety, recorded to encourage emulation: which examples are the finest? Among those who fully realized the Five Relationships, who may serve as models? Set this out clearly in your essay, concealing nothing.

Question: In learning, nothing takes precedence over investigating principle. Mind, human nature, sincerity, and reverence are all matters whose principles must be investigated. Let us discuss them together. The great Shun opened the source of the learning of the mind for all ages, and subsequent thinkers who discussed the mind took him as their progenitor. Cheng Tang revealed the profound meaning of the learning of human nature for all ages, and subsequent thinkers who discussed human nature took him as their progenitor. The mind is one: why, then, are there such differing formulations as the human mind, the mind of the Way, the mind as the Supreme Ultimate, and the mind as the wondrous integration of nature and feelings? Human nature is one: why, then, are there distinctions involving Heaven’s endowment, material constitution, goodness and evil, and the three grades? The Six Classics contain statements about sincerity and statements about reverence. Yet it has been said that since the Han no one has understood the word “sincerity.” Some earlier Confucian scholars explained it as not deceiving, some as never ceasing, and some as being without falsity. Which explanation fully encompasses it? It has been said that since the Qin no one has understood the word “reverence.” Some earlier Confucian scholars explained it as being orderly, composed, strict, and solemn; some as the method of remaining constantly alert; and some as gathering in the mind so that it admits not a single thing. Which explanation is complete? Can mind, human nature, sincerity, and reverence truly be threaded together by a single principle? You candidates have devoted years to study and discussion. Please unravel these matters in your replies.

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
譏也試與諸士子論之文之體有詔制
誥初所命表箋者有碑碣誄誌記序傳
解者有論疏辯說簡狀啓檄露布劄子
者詩之體有辭賦騷選雅操箴銘者有
歌曲行引謠吟古律者有側抝篇詠言
謳嘆怨樂府者其命義安在果有得於
經之體歟以文而論或辯賢良策或爲
過秦論或作王命論或作美新或記蘭
亭可謂盛矣何前賢獨取孔明之表歟
===
以詩而論或高妙或冲淡或豪邁或峻
潔或華麗可謂美矣何先正獨取子美
之詩歟我
朝文運亨嘉上自臺閣下及衡門之士含英
咀華發於詩文率足以鳴
國家之盛視前代諸賢著作孰優孰劣必有
能辯之者幸明言之
聞有一代之人物必有一代之名譽天下
之公論係焉雖平不可誣已唐虞三代
punctuated:
譏也。試與諸士子論之。文之體有詔、制、誥、初所命、表、箋者，有碑、碣、誄、誌、記、序、傳、解者，有論、疏、辯、說、簡、狀、啓、檄、露布、劄子者。詩之體有辭、賦、騷、選、雅、操、箴、銘者，有歌、曲、行、引、謠、吟、古、律者，有側、抝、篇、詠、言、謳、嘆、怨、樂府者。其命義安在？果有得於經之體歟？以文而論，或辯賢良策，或爲《過秦論》，或作《王命論》，或作《美新》，或記蘭亭，可謂盛矣。何前賢獨取孔明之表歟？以詩而論，或高妙，或冲淡，或豪邁，或峻潔，或華麗，可謂美矣。何先正獨取子美之詩歟？我朝文運亨嘉，上自臺閣，下及衡門之士，含英咀華，發於詩文，率足以鳴國家之盛。視前代諸賢著作，孰優孰劣？必有能辯之者，幸明言之。

聞有一代之人物，必有一代之名譽，天下之公論係焉，雖平不可誣已。唐虞三代
translation_en:
…be subjected to critical appraisal. Let us discuss this with you candidates. Among the forms of prose are imperial edicts, decrees, proclamations, “chu suo ming” [?], formal memorials, and letters of homage; stele inscriptions, stone-marker inscriptions, eulogies for the dead, epitaphs, records, prefaces, biographies, and elucidations; discourses, memorials presenting arguments, disputations, explanations, letters, statements, communications to superiors, military proclamations, open proclamations, and memoranda. Among the forms of poetry are lyric compositions, rhapsodies, sao poems, “selections,” elegant odes, zither songs, admonitions, and inscriptions; songs, tunes, ballads, introductory songs, folk songs, chants, ancient-style verse, and regulated verse; and “oblique” and “contorted” verse [?], pieces, poetic celebrations, “utterances,” songs of praise, laments, plaints, and Music Bureau poems. What meanings underlie these names? Do these forms truly partake of the forms of the Classics?

In prose, some expounded policy answers for the Worthy and Good examination, some composed the Discourse on the Faults of Qin, some wrote the Discourse on the Mandate of Kings, some wrote In Praise of the Xin Dynasty, and some recorded the gathering at Lanting. These may be called flourishing achievements. Why, then, did earlier worthies single out Kongming’s memorial? In poetry, some works are lofty and subtle, some serene and understated, some bold and unrestrained, some austere and pure, and some ornate and splendid. These may be called beautiful achievements. Why, then, did earlier sages single out the poetry of Zimei?

Under our dynasty, literary fortunes flourish auspiciously. From officials in the central government down to scholars dwelling behind humble gates, men savor literary blossoms and express themselves in poetry and prose, their works generally sufficing to proclaim the flourishing of the state. Compared with the writings of the worthies of previous ages, which are superior and which inferior? Surely there are those who can distinguish them. Please explain clearly.

We have heard that every age has its notable figures and necessarily its own reputations, upon which the impartial judgment of the world bears. “Although level” [?], these cannot be falsified. The ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
之人物名實相孚文德攸濟國不以論
矣自漢以來有名著於朝廷者誰歟有
名顯於天下者誰歟名揚於郡國與鄉
於外域者可指言歟名形於謳詠與見
於並稱者可悉數歟他如名在於潔目
係於地理者又可得而知其人歟夫子
之學務實而已何以名爲諸生抱負實
學有素於前之諸君子其以何人爲法
歟言及之而不言君子不爲也
===
問天下事可言者多矣試舉其切於時宜
者相與商確之在昔用能授官歲計吏
治今任賢去邪之法猶是也然一有剌
舉賢否混淆登用者未必皆賢被黜者
未必皆否伊欲黜陟公而賢否不混
淆何法以處之古者田以井授稅以什
一今足國裕民之計猶古也然一有調
發公私困乏即隋胃宜盡斷於富室實
係耀斂每困於荊僚伊欲用度足而公
punctuated:
之人物，名實相孚，文德攸濟，國不以論矣。自漢以來，有名著於朝廷者誰歟？有名顯於天下者誰歟？名揚於郡國與鄉於外域者，可指言歟？名形於謳詠與見於並稱者，可悉數歟？他如名在於潔目、係於地理者，又可得而知其人歟？夫子之學，務實而已，何以名爲？諸生抱負實學有素，於前之諸君子，其以何人爲法歟？言及之而不言，君子不爲也。

問：天下事可言者多矣，試舉其切於時宜者，相與商確之。在昔用能授官，歲計吏治，今任賢去邪之法猶是也。然一有剌舉，賢否混淆，登用者未必皆賢，被黜者未必皆否。伊欲黜陟公而賢否不混淆，何法以處之？古者田以井授，稅以什一，今足國裕民之計猶古也。然一有調發，公私困乏，即隋胃宜盡斷於富室，實係耀斂，每困於荊僚。伊欲用度足而公
translation_en:
…the men of those times possessed reputations that accorded with their actual merits, and brought their civil virtues to fruition; they need not be discussed [?]. Since the Han, whose reputations have been celebrated at court? Whose have been renowned throughout the realm? Can you identify those whose fame spread through the commanderies and kingdoms and reached foreign lands [?]? Can you enumerate all those whose names appeared in songs of praise or were mentioned together with those of others? As for those whose names appear in lists [?] or are associated with geographical features, can their identities also be known? The Master's learning sought substance alone; what use had he for fame? You students have long cultivated substantial learning. Which of the gentlemen mentioned above would you take as your model? To withhold one's words when the discussion calls for them is something a gentleman does not do.

Question: There are many affairs in the realm worth discussing. Let us select those most pertinent to present needs and examine them together. In antiquity, men were appointed to office according to their abilities, and officials' administration was assessed annually. Today's methods of employing the worthy and removing the wicked follow the same principle. Yet whenever officials are investigated and impeached, the worthy and unworthy become confused: those promoted are not necessarily all worthy, nor are those dismissed necessarily all unworthy. If we wish to make dismissal and promotion impartial and prevent confusion between the worthy and unworthy, by what method should we proceed? In antiquity, fields were allotted under the well-field system, and a tenth was collected in tax. Today's plans to provide sufficient resources for the state and prosperity for the people follow those of antiquity. Yet whenever requisitions are imposed, both public and private resources are exhausted. [The following passage is garbled:] … should all be determined with reference to wealthy households [?]; in fact, it concerns levies and collections [?], and difficulties repeatedly arise from subordinate officials [?]. If we wish to ensure sufficient funds for expenditure while public …

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
私不至困之何道以致之守令民之師
帥所以承流而宣化者也今
朝廷以守令惟取于監牘慮六事或未脩也
故兼選進士出補郡邑無非欲得人以
安黎庶而已何以能使馴雉卻虎之良
不垂耳於鹽車乎將帥民之保障所使
以身而運臂者也今
朝廷以將帥惟取於世襲慮才德或未諳也
故請開武舉兼試文藝無非欲得人以
===
衛疆埸而已何以能使販繒屠狗之輩
不落魄於閭閻乎昔范希文自做秀才
時便以天下為己任爾諸生飽飫經史
豈無懷用世之志如希文者願著于篇
以俟聞于
上
punctuated: 私不至困之，何道以致之？守令，民之師帥，所以承流而宣化者也。今朝廷以守令惟取于監牘，慮六事或未脩也，故兼選進士出補郡邑，無非欲得人以安黎庶而已。何以能使馴雉卻虎之良，不垂耳於鹽車乎？將帥，民之保障，所使以身而運臂者也。今朝廷以將帥惟取於世襲，慮才德或未諳也，故請開武舉，兼試文藝，無非欲得人以衛疆埸而已。何以能使販繒屠狗之輩，不落魄於閭閻乎？昔范希文自做秀才時，便以天下為己任。爾諸生飽飫經史，豈無懷用世之志如希文者？願著于篇，以俟聞于上。
translation_en:
…and private resources do not become exhausted—by what means can this be achieved? Prefects and county magistrates are the people’s teachers and leaders, through whom the court’s influence flows and its transforming instruction is disseminated. Now the court, considering that recruiting prefects and county magistrates solely from official registers [?] might leave the six duties unfulfilled, also selects metropolitan graduates (jinshi) for appointments in prefectures and counties. Its sole purpose is to obtain suitable men to bring peace to the common people. How can we ensure that worthy officials capable of taming pheasants and driving away tigers do not droop their ears like fine horses harnessed to salt carts?

Generals and commanders are the people’s protection, to be directed as the body moves its arms. Now the court, considering that recruiting generals and commanders solely through hereditary succession might leave their ability and virtue insufficiently known, has therefore requested the establishment of military examinations that also test literary accomplishment. Its sole purpose is to obtain suitable men to defend the frontiers. How can we ensure that men who sell silk or slaughter dogs do not languish in obscurity among the common people?

In former times, Fan Xiwen, from his days as a student, already took responsibility for all under Heaven upon himself. You students have steeped yourselves in the classics and histories: are there none among you who cherish an ambition to serve the world as Xiwen did? Set forth your thoughts in writing, so that they may be brought to His Majesty’s attention.

於吾身根於其德仁極仁義極義凡見於望
者皆仁義之發越禮極禮智極智凡形諸言
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

故君子之道，本諸身，徵諸庶民，考諸三王而不謬，建諸天地而不悖，質諸鬼神而無疑，百世以俟聖人而不惑。

鮑璉

考試官學正章，批〔理明詞暢，且分畫不差，作手也。〕

考試官教授鄭，批〔辭理詳盡，是宜錄出。〕

論王者之制作，本於德而所驗無不合也。蓋制作，所以王天下之道也。茍非本於德而驗之無不合，又何以行於天下也哉？今夫人君中天下而立，定四海之民，其王天下之道在乎議禮、制度、考文而已。議禮以同其倫，制度以同其軌，考文以同其文。所以新天下之視聽者在是，所以一天下之心志者在是，可不本於德乎？必也本於吾身，根於其德。仁極仁，義極義，凡見於望者，皆仁義之發越；禮極禮，智極智，凡形諸言
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Thus the gentleman’s Way is rooted in his own person and verified among the common people. Tested against the Three Kings, it proves free of error; established before Heaven and Earth, it does not conflict with them; questioned before the spirits, it leaves no doubt. He can await a sage a hundred generations hence without uncertainty.”

Bao Lian

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔The principles are clear and the language fluent; moreover, the distinctions are correctly drawn. This is an accomplished writer.〕

Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: 〔The expression and reasoning are thorough. This deserves to be selected for inclusion.〕

The argument is that a true king’s establishment of institutions is rooted in virtue and accords with every test applied to it. For establishing institutions is the means by which a king rules all under Heaven. Unless these institutions were rooted in virtue and accorded with every test, how could they be put into practice throughout the realm? Now, the ruler stands at the center of all under Heaven and brings stability to the people within the Four Seas. His way of ruling all under Heaven consists simply in deliberating on ritual, establishing regulations, and examining written forms. He deliberates on ritual to unify social relationships, establishes regulations to unify standards, and examines written forms to unify writing. Herein lies the means of renewing what all under Heaven see and hear; herein lies the means of unifying their hearts and purposes. Could these things fail to be rooted in virtue? They must be grounded in his own person and rooted in his virtue. Benevolence must reach the utmost in benevolence, and righteousness the utmost in righteousness: everything visible in his appearance [?] is an expression of benevolence and righteousness. Ritual propriety must reach the utmost in ritual propriety, and wisdom the utmost in wisdom: everything expressed in words…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
者智禮智之流行由是驗之於民是矜是式而
無不從徵之於人是遵是守而無不信三王已
行之迹以是道而考之則與之脗合而無所差
天地自然之道以是道而參之則與之默契而
無所悖無形而難知者鬼神也以之而質諸鬼
神則幽有以驗乎明而無疑焉未至而難料者
後聖也以之而俟諸後聖則遠有以驗乎近而
不惑焉吁君子之道本之有其德驗之無不合
此其所以爲王天下者之所重歟雖然中庸此
===
章首明居上不驕之意而言及此以見王者之
制作不惟本於其德又必達幽明貫古今而無
不合斯能行之天下而致聲譽於無窮焉不然
下文何以曰君子未有不如此而蚤有譽於天
下者也因併及之
我非堯舜之道不敢以陳於王前故齊人
莫如我敬王也
高嶽
同考試官訓導李　批　詞□□□□□
punctuated:
者，智禮智之流行。由是驗之於民，是矜是式，而無不從；徵之於人，是遵是守，而無不信。三王已行之迹，以是道而考之，則與之脗合而無所差；天地自然之道，以是道而參之，則與之默契而無所悖。無形而難知者，鬼神也；以之而質諸鬼神，則幽有以驗乎明而無疑焉。未至而難料者，後聖也；以之而俟諸後聖，則遠有以驗乎近而不惑焉。吁！君子之道，本之有其德，驗之無不合，此其所以爲王天下者之所重歟？雖然，《中庸》此章首明居上不驕之意，而言及此，以見王者之制作，不惟本於其德，又必達幽明、貫古今而無不合，斯能行之天下而致聲譽於無窮焉。不然，下文何以曰：「君子未有不如此而蚤有譽於天下者也」？因併及之。
我非堯舜之道，不敢以陳於王前，故齊人莫如我敬王也。
高嶽
同考試官訓導李　批：詞□□□□□
translation_en:
…are the flowing expression of wisdom, ritual propriety, and wisdom [?]. Thus, when tested among the people, they take it as their model and standard, and none fail to follow it; when verified among others, they observe and uphold it, and none fail to trust it. If the established precedents of the Three Kings are examined by this Way, it accords with them without discrepancy. If the spontaneous Way of Heaven and Earth is compared with this Way, it accords with it tacitly, without contradiction. Spirits are formless and difficult to know; yet if this Way is submitted to the spirits for judgment, the hidden can verify the manifest, leaving no doubt. Future sages have not yet appeared and are difficult to anticipate; yet if this Way awaits their judgment, the distant can verify the near, leaving no uncertainty. Ah! The gentleman’s Way is grounded in his virtue and, wherever tested, proves consonant. Is this not why those who rule all under Heaven esteem it?
Nevertheless, this chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean begins by explaining what it means to occupy a high position without arrogance, and then proceeds to this point. It thereby shows that a king’s institutions must not only be grounded in his virtue, but must also encompass the hidden and the manifest and extend through past and present, proving consonant everywhere. Only then can they be put into practice throughout the realm and bring him a reputation without end. Otherwise, why would the subsequent passage say, “Never has a gentleman gained an early reputation throughout the realm without being like this”? Accordingly, I have discussed this point as well.
“If it is not the Way of Yao and Shun, I dare not set it forth before the king. Thus, among the people of Qi, none respects the king as I do.”
Gao Yue.

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
佳作也
同考試官教諭董　批　以仁義立說詞然孟子告君之意且筆力蒼古非初學可到
考試官學正章　批　詞健理明讀之令人起敬
考試官教授鄭　批　說孟子告齊王之意宛然當時氣象健美健美
大賢自言以前聖之道告其君非時人之所能
及也蓋堯舜之道仁義之道也大賢以是而告
===
君則敬君之心至矣又豈時人之所能企及哉
昔孟子因景子譏己不見齊王而告之若曰奔
走承順齊人敬君之小也我之責難於君非常
堯仁義之道則不敢言於前外此而功利之說
不言也聲踸曲拳齊人敬君以貌也我之陳善
於君非帝舜仁義之道亦不敢言於前舍此而
甲兵之事不言也言焉而堯言焉而舜非好迂
也非過望也蓋欲以吾君體帝堯仁義之心平
章百姓協和萬邦不堯其君不止焉行帝舜仁
punctuated:
佳作也。
同考試官教諭董批：以仁義立說，詞然孟子告君之意，且筆力蒼古，非初學可到。
考試官學正章批：詞健理明，讀之令人起敬。
考試官教授鄭批：說孟子告齊王之意，宛然當時氣象。健美！健美！
大賢自言，以前聖之道告其君，非時人之所能及也。蓋堯舜之道，仁義之道也。大賢以是而告君，則敬君之心至矣，又豈時人之所能企及哉！昔孟子因景子譏己不見齊王而告之，若曰：「奔走承順，齊人敬君之小也。我之責難於君，非常堯仁義之道，則不敢言於前；外此而功利之說，不言也。聲踸曲拳，齊人敬君以貌也。我之陳善於君，非帝舜仁義之道，亦不敢言於前；舍此而甲兵之事，不言也。言焉而堯，言焉而舜，非好迂也，非過望也。蓋欲以吾君體帝堯仁義之心，平章百姓，協和萬邦，不堯其君不止焉；行帝舜仁
translation_en:
…a fine composition.
Associate Examiner Dong, Instructor, comments: “It grounds its argument in benevolence and righteousness and conveys [?] Mencius’s intention in addressing his ruler. Moreover, its writing has an antique vigor beyond the reach of a beginner.”
Examiner Zhang, School Director, comments: “The language is vigorous and the reasoning clear. Reading it inspires respect.”
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: “It explains Mencius’s intention in addressing the king of Qi, vividly evoking the spirit of that time. Vigorous and beautiful! Vigorous and beautiful!”
The great worthy himself declared that, in presenting the Way of the former sages to his ruler, he did what his contemporaries could not match. For the Way of Yao and Shun is the Way of benevolence and righteousness. By presenting this to his ruler, the great worthy showed the utmost reverence for him. How could his contemporaries ever hope to equal it?
Once, when Jingzi reproached Mencius for not going to see the king of Qi, Mencius answered him in words to this effect: “Hurrying to serve and submissively complying are the lesser ways in which the people of Qi revere their ruler. In demanding difficult achievements of my ruler, I dare present nothing before him except the Way of benevolence and righteousness of Yao [?]. Beyond this, I will not speak of profit and advantage. Adopting deferential sounds and bent postures [?] is how the people of Qi revere their ruler through outward appearances. In setting goodness before my ruler, I likewise dare present nothing before him except Emperor Shun’s Way of benevolence and righteousness. Apart from this, I will not speak of arms and warfare. That whenever I speak I invoke Yao, and whenever I speak I invoke Shun, is neither a fondness for impracticality nor excessive expectation. Rather, I wish my ruler to embody Emperor Yao’s heart of benevolence and righteousness, bring order and distinction to the hundred clans, and harmonize the myriad states. I will not cease until I have made my ruler a Yao; and to practice Emperor Shun’s benevolence …

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
義之道五典克從百揆時敘不舜其君不止焉
彼齊人舍其大而務其小豈如我敬君之大乎
以其貌而不以其心豈如我敬君之至乎吁不
以戰國之君視其君而以堯舜之君望其君若
孟子者可不為萬世人臣之龜鑑歟雖然時而
戰國人皆不知性之本善故孟子道性善言必
稱堯舜是以一書之中拳拳以堯舜稱之則知
堯舜不獨為人君之法臣道也父道也子道也
兄弟也朋友也何莫而不以堯舜為法乎
===
易
觀乎人文以化成天下
高嶽
同考試官訓導李 批〔發明實道之大是作〕
得之
同考試官教諭童 批〔作此題者於觀人文處多忽畧於化成處多陳腐是篇說理詳盡而〕
〔備腐為新當是作手〕
考試官學正章 批〔易義體認明白佳〕
punctuated:
義之道，五典克從，百揆時敘，不舜其君不止焉。彼齊人舍其大而務其小，豈如我敬君之大乎？以其貌而不以其心，豈如我敬君之至乎？吁！不以戰國之君視其君，而以堯舜之君望其君，若孟子者，可不為萬世人臣之龜鑑歟？雖然，時而戰國，人皆不知性之本善，故孟子道性善，言必稱堯舜。是以一書之中，拳拳以堯舜稱之，則知堯舜不獨為人君之法，臣道也，父道也，子道也，兄弟也，朋友也，何莫而不以堯舜為法乎？

易
觀乎人文，以化成天下。
高嶽

同考試官訓導李，批〔發明實道之大，是作〕得之。

同考試官教諭童，批〔作此題者，於觀人文處多忽畧，於化成處多陳腐。是篇說理詳盡，而〕〔備腐為新，當是作手。〕

考試官學正章，批〔易義體認明白，佳〕
translation_en:
…the way of righteousness, so that the five constant human relationships are duly observed and the hundred affairs of government are properly ordered; he will not rest until he has made his ruler a Shun. Those people of Qi neglect what is great and attend to what is small: how could their respect for their ruler equal mine in its greatness? They show it outwardly rather than in their hearts: how could their respect for their ruler equal mine in its utmost sincerity? Ah! He does not regard his ruler merely as a ruler of the Warring States, but expects him to become a ruler like Yao or Shun. Could someone like Mengzi not serve as a guide and mirror for ministers throughout all ages? Nevertheless, in the Warring States period, people did not understand the original goodness of human nature. Thus, when Mengzi spoke of the goodness of human nature, he invariably cited Yao and Shun. Throughout his book, he earnestly and repeatedly invokes them. From this we know that Yao and Shun are models not only for rulers. In the ways of ministers, fathers, sons, brothers, and friends, where should one not take Yao and Shun as models?

Book of Changes
“Observe human cultural patterns, thereby transforming and perfecting all under Heaven.”
Gao Yue

Associate Examiner Tong, Instructor, comments: “Those who write on this topic often neglect the passage about observing human cultural patterns, while their treatment of transformation and perfection is often stale. This essay explains the principles thoroughly and turns the stale into the fresh [?]. Its author must be an accomplished writer.”

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of the Changes is clearly grasped. An excellent…”

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
作也
考試官教授鄭　批　發明賁道得聖人作
易之意
觀人道之賁成世道之賁蓋易卦文明以止此
人道之賁也聖人觀之以化成天下豈非世道
之賁乎彖傳聖人極言賁道之大如此且夫賁
之為卦離明於內艮止於外文明以止人之文
也聖人果何以觀之而化成天下乎誠以父子
君臣繳然有禮以相接而尊卑之分不踰此人
===
之文也夫婦長幼朋友秩然有禮以相與而上
下之分不瀆亦人之文也聖人為人文之主宰
觀在易之人文以之而化成天下篤之以恩限
之以分舊者化而新久而成其俗由是天下之
為父子為君臣者莫不有親有義而父子君臣
同一人文之化也天下之為夫婦為長幼為朋
友者莫不有別有序有信而夫婦長幼朋友同
一人文之化也家不殊俗人人有君子之行國
不異政比屋有可封之俗天下之大一人文之
punctuated:
作也。

考試官教授鄭批：發明賁道，得聖人作《易》之意。

觀人道之賁，成世道之賁。蓋《易》卦文明以止，此人道之賁也。聖人觀之以化成天下，豈非世道之賁乎？《彖傳》聖人極言賁道之大如此。且夫賁之為卦，離明於內，艮止於外，文明以止，人之文也。聖人果何以觀之而化成天下乎？誠以父子君臣繳然有禮以相接，而尊卑之分不踰，此人之文也；夫婦長幼朋友秩然有禮以相與，而上下之分不瀆，亦人之文也。聖人為人文之主宰，觀在《易》之人文，以之而化成天下。篤之以恩，限之以分，舊者化而新，久而成其俗。由是天下之為父子、為君臣者，莫不有親有義，而父子君臣同一人文之化也；天下之為夫婦、為長幼、為朋友者，莫不有別有序有信，而夫婦長幼朋友同一人文之化也。家不殊俗，人人有君子之行；國不異政，比屋有可封之俗。天下之大，一人文之
translation_en:
…composition.

Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: “This elucidates the Way of Adornment and grasps the sage’s intention in composing the Book of Changes.”

By observing the adornment of human relationships, one brings the adornment of the social order to completion. In the hexagram of the Book of Changes, cultural illumination is held within bounds: this is the adornment of human relationships. The sage observes it in order to transform all under Heaven and bring them to fulfillment. Is this not the adornment of the social order? Such is the fullness with which the sage, in the Commentary on the Judgments, describes the greatness of the Way of Adornment. Now, in the hexagram Adornment (Bi), Li provides illumination within, and Gen provides restraint without. Cultural illumination held within bounds constitutes human culture. How, then, does the sage observe this and thereby transform all under Heaven and bring them to fulfillment?

Indeed, fathers and sons, rulers and ministers, interact according to ritual in an orderly manner [?], without overstepping the distinctions between honored and humble: this is human culture. Husbands and wives, elders and juniors, and friends deal with one another in an orderly manner according to ritual, without confusing the distinctions between higher and lower: this too is human culture. As the presiding authority over human culture, the sage observes human culture as presented in the Book of Changes and uses it to transform all under Heaven and bring them to fulfillment. He strengthens their bonds through kindness and sets limits through the distinctions proper to their relationships. What is old is transformed and renewed, and over time this becomes their custom.

Thus, throughout all under Heaven, fathers and sons, rulers and ministers, invariably possess affection and righteousness; fathers and sons, rulers and ministers alike share in the transforming influence of human culture. Throughout all under Heaven, husbands and wives, elders and juniors, and friends invariably maintain distinction, order, and trustworthiness; husbands and wives, elders and juniors, and friends alike share in the transforming influence of human culture. Families do not differ in their customs, and everyone conducts himself as a gentleman. States do not differ in their governance, and the prevailing customs are such that every household has someone worthy of enfeoffment. Across the vastness of all under Heaven, a single human culture’s…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
化成世道之責孰有加於此哉大抵天下之道
莫大於人倫人君負天下之道莫大於明倫人
倫明於上則小民親於下矣堯舜之所以帝禹
湯文武之所以王用此責也然則負道之大非
聖人其孰能用之乎
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
與剛立人之道曰仁與義兼三才而兩
之故易六畫而成卦分陰分陽迭用柔
剛故易六位而成章
許銳
===
同考試官訓導李　批〔此題場中作者多分截不明且陳腐可厭脫得是篇深合題意允宜錄出以〕
破群蒙
同考試官教諭童　批〔性命之理即三才之道六畫之成卦成章皆所以順乎此理也是作體認親切〕
分截允當一洗易學之舊習閱之心目豁然
考試官學正章　批〔是篇得聖人說卦之旨〕
punctuated:
化成。世道之責，孰有加於此哉？大抵天下之道，莫大於人倫；人君負天下之道，莫大於明倫。人倫明於上，則小民親於下矣。堯舜之所以帝，禹湯文武之所以王，用此責也。然則負道之大，非聖人，其孰能用之乎？

昔者聖人之作易也，將以順性命之理，是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。

許銳

同考試官訓導李，批〔此題場中作者多分截不明，且陳腐可厭。脫得是篇，深合題意，允宜錄出，以〕破群蒙。

同考試官教諭童，批〔性命之理，即三才之道；六畫之成卦成章，皆所以順乎此理也。是作體認親切，〕分截允當，一洗易學之舊習，閱之心目豁然。

考試官學正章，批〔是篇得聖人說卦之旨。〕
translation_en:
… transformed and brought to completion. What responsibility for the moral order of the world could exceed this? Broadly speaking, nothing in the Way of the world is greater than human relationships; in a ruler’s responsibility for that Way, nothing is greater than making those relationships clear. When human relationships are clarified above, the common people below become affectionate toward one another. It was by fulfilling this responsibility that Yao and Shun ruled as emperors, and Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu ruled as kings. Who but a sage, then, could discharge so great a responsibility for the Way?

“In ancient times, when the sages made the Changes, they intended thereby to accord with the principles of human nature and destiny. Thus they established the Way of Heaven as yin and yang, the Way of Earth as yielding and firm, and the Way of humanity as benevolence and righteousness. They combined the Three Powers and doubled them; hence, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. They distinguished yin and yang and employed yielding and firm in alternation; hence, in the Changes, the six positions form an ordered pattern.”

Xu Rui 許銳

Comment by Associate Examiner Li 李, Assistant Instructor: “Among those who wrote on this topic in the examination, many failed to distinguish its divisions clearly, and their writing was stale and tiresome. Coming upon this essay [?], which accords closely with the topic’s meaning, we certainly ought to select and reproduce it to dispel the ignorance of the many.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Tong 童, Instructor: “The principles of human nature and destiny are precisely the Way of the Three Powers. The six lines’ formation of hexagrams and ordered patterns serves in every case to accord with these principles. This composition shows an intimate understanding; its divisions are entirely appropriate. It sweeps away the ingrained habits of studying the Changes: reading it opens both mind and eyes.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang 章, Instructor: “This essay grasps the sage’s purport in ‘Explaining the Trigrams.’”

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授鄭　批〔此作說理詳明蓋精　於易學者〕
聖人易書之作欲以順乎理故易畫之備有以
順乎理蓋性命之理卽三才之道也聖人作易
兼三才而成卦問六位而成章何莫而非所以
順乎是理也歟嘗觀吾夫子說卦之意謂夫昔
者聖人之作易也豈徒具卦爻之象哉將以順
性命之理而已彼性命之理出於一原而散見
於三才者也是以立天之道曰陰與陽而陰陽
===
固此性命之理也立地之道曰柔與剛而剛柔
亦此性命之理也立人之道曰仁與義而仁義
孰非此性命之理乎惟理不外乎三才故卦必
成於六畫故聖人作易總而言之兼天之道而
兩之則五為天之陽上為天之陰兼地之道而
兩之則初為地之剛二為地之柔兼人道而兩
之則三為人之仁四為人之義兩者既兼六者
斯備而易之卦體以全細而分之初三五為陽
位二四上為陰位而陰陽中分位之陽者為剛
punctuated:
考試官教授鄭　批〔此作說理詳明，蓋精　於易學者。〕

聖人易書之作，欲以順乎理，故易畫之備，有以順乎理。蓋性命之理卽三才之道也。聖人作易，兼三才而成卦，問六位而成章，何莫而非所以順乎是理也歟？嘗觀吾夫子說卦之意，謂夫昔者聖人之作易也，豈徒具卦爻之象哉？將以順性命之理而已。彼性命之理，出於一原而散見於三才者也。是以立天之道曰陰與陽，而陰陽固此性命之理也；立地之道曰柔與剛，而剛柔亦此性命之理也；立人之道曰仁與義，而仁義孰非此性命之理乎？惟理不外乎三才，故卦必成於六畫。故聖人作易，總而言之，兼天之道而兩之，則五為天之陽，上為天之陰；兼地之道而兩之，則初為地之剛，二為地之柔；兼人道而兩之，則三為人之仁，四為人之義。兩者既兼，六者斯備，而易之卦體以全。細而分之，初三五為陽位，二四上為陰位，而陰陽中分，位之陽者為剛。
translation_en:
Examiner Zheng, an instructor, comments: 〔This composition expounds the principles clearly and thoroughly. Its author is evidently proficient in the study of the Changes.〕

In composing the Book of Changes, the sages intended to accord with principle; thus the full complement of its lines provides the means to accord with principle. The principles of human nature and destiny are precisely the Way of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity. The sages composed the Changes, encompassing the Three Powers to form hexagrams and, through the six positions [?], producing patterned distinctions. How could any of this fail to serve the purpose of according with these principles?

I have considered the meaning of our Master’s Explanation of the Hexagrams. It says that when the sages of antiquity composed the Changes, their purpose was surely not merely to furnish images of hexagrams and individual lines. They intended only to accord with the principles of human nature and destiny. These principles issue from a single source and are manifested variously in the Three Powers. Thus, in establishing the Way of Heaven, they named yin and yang; and yin and yang are indeed these very principles of human nature and destiny. In establishing the Way of Earth, they named yielding and firm; and firmness and yielding are likewise these principles. In establishing the Way of humanity, they named benevolence and righteousness; and which of these is not an expression of these principles?

Since principle does not lie outside the Three Powers, a hexagram must be formed from six lines. Thus, when the sages composed the Changes, considered as a whole, they encompassed the Way of Heaven and doubled it: the fifth position represents Heaven’s yang, and the top position Heaven’s yin. They encompassed the Way of Earth and doubled it: the first position represents Earth’s firmness, and the second Earth’s yielding. They encompassed the Way of humanity and doubled it: the third position represents human benevolence, and the fourth human righteousness. Once both aspects of each were encompassed, all six were present, and the hexagram structure of the Changes was complete. Distinguished in detail, the first, third, and fifth are yang positions, while the second, fourth, and top are yin positions. Yin and yang are thus equally divided; those positions that are yang are firm …

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
位之陰者爲柔而剛柔迭用陰陽相閒剛柔相
雜而易之文章以著卦畫之成者此理也文章
之著者此理也聖人作易以順性命之理豈不
於此而可見乎大抵易之未作性命之理見於
三才易之既作三才之道具於卦畫見於三才
之理即具於卦畫之理故吾夫子贊易一則曰
六爻之動三極之道也一則曰六者非他也三
才之道也至此又以是發明之先儒謂易者性
命之原蓋亦有見於斯云
===
書
從諫弗咈先民時若居上克明爲下克忠
與人不求備檢身若不及
劉鎡
同考試官訓導陳　批〔此篇發明成湯脩人紀之實節節分明殆無餘蘊佳作也〕
同考試官訓導曾　批〔於經也明於文也整本房書義之踞外此夫何求〕
同考試官教諭劉　批〔題本平易作者固多〕
punctuated:
位之陰者爲柔，而剛柔迭用，陰陽相閒，剛柔相雜，而易之文章以著。卦畫之成者，此理也；文章之著者，此理也。聖人作易，以順性命之理，豈不於此而可見乎？大抵易之未作，性命之理見於三才；易之既作，三才之道具於卦畫。見於三才之理，即具於卦畫之理。故吾夫子贊易，一則曰：「六爻之動，三極之道也。」一則曰：「六者非他也，三才之道也。」至此又以是發明之。先儒謂易者性命之原，蓋亦有見於斯云。

書
從諫弗咈，先民時若。居上克明，爲下克忠。與人不求備，檢身若不及。
劉鎡
同考試官訓導陳　批〔此篇發明成湯脩人紀之實，節節分明，殆無餘蘊，佳作也。〕
同考試官訓導曾　批〔於經也明，於文也整，本房書義之踞，外此夫何求？〕
同考試官教諭劉　批〔題本平易，作者固多〕
translation_en:
…Those occupying yin positions are yielding. The firm and the yielding operate in alternation; yin and yang are interspersed, and the firm and the yielding intermingle, so that the patterned configurations of the Changes become manifest. It is this principle that forms the hexagram lines; it is this principle that makes their patterns manifest. Can we not see here how the sages made the Changes to accord with the principle of human nature and destiny? In general, before the Changes was made, the principle of human nature and destiny was manifest in the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity. Once the Changes was made, the Way of the Three Powers was embodied in the hexagram lines. The principle manifest in the Three Powers is precisely the principle embodied in those lines. Thus, in his commentary on the Changes, our Master Confucius says in one place, “The movements of the six lines are the Way of the Three Ultimates,” and in another, “The six are nothing other than the Way of the Three Powers.” Here again he elucidates it through this same idea. Earlier Confucian scholars called the Changes the source of human nature and destiny; surely they too perceived something of this.

Book of Documents
“Follow remonstrance without opposing it, and conform to the men of old. When occupying a superior position, be discerning; when serving below, be loyal. Do not demand perfection of others; examine yourself as though you had not done enough.”
Liu Zi 劉鎡

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: 〔This essay elucidates the substance of Cheng Tang’s cultivation of human relationships. Every successive point is clearly distinguished, leaving scarcely anything unexplored. An excellent composition.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng, Assistant Instructor: 〔Clear in its understanding of the Classic and orderly in its composition, this stands foremost [?] among the essays on the Book of Documents in this examining room. What more could one seek?〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔The topic itself is straightforward, and many have indeed written on it…〕

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
〔求其詞理兼盡者僅見此篇〕
考試官學正章　批　〔得成湯脩人紀之實而措詞詳盡作手也〕
考試官教授鄭　批　〔六事皆湯之自脩此篇以人紀貫講得之〕
隨所事而各盡其道此前聖脩人紀然也蓋前
聖以人紀為一身之任故脩之之功隨所事而
各盡其道大臣舉以為賢王告其忠愛之意不
既深乎昔伊尹欲太甲立愛敬而謹厥始故告
===
之以此若曰先王成湯肇脩人紀果何以見之
哉彼其忠言讜論所以扶持人紀者也則樂善
不倦從之而弗逆焉前輩舊德所以倡率人紀
者也則見善必從順之而不悖焉居上也則以
人紀之道躬行於臨御之時而無一毫之或肆
使在下有所視效其克明也何如為下也則以
人紀之道敷陳於納誨之際而無一息之或欺
使在上有所箴規其克忠也何如在人或能脩
人紀也則惟善是取不責以他德之未全何嘗
punctuated:
〔求其詞理兼盡者，僅見此篇。〕
考試官學正章　批〔得成湯脩人紀之實，而措詞詳盡，作手也。〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔六事皆湯之自脩，此篇以人紀貫講，得之。〕

隨所事而各盡其道，此前聖脩人紀然也。蓋前聖以人紀為一身之任，故脩之之功，隨所事而各盡其道。大臣舉以為賢王告，其忠愛之意，不既深乎？昔伊尹欲太甲立愛敬而謹厥始，故告之以此，若曰：「先王成湯肇脩人紀，果何以見之哉？彼其忠言讜論，所以扶持人紀者也，則樂善不倦，從之而弗逆焉；前輩舊德，所以倡率人紀者也，則見善必從，順之而不悖焉。居上也，則以人紀之道躬行於臨御之時，而無一毫之或肆，使在下有所視效，其克明也何如！為下也，則以人紀之道敷陳於納誨之際，而無一息之或欺，使在上有所箴規，其克忠也何如！在人或能脩人紀也，則惟善是取，不責以他德之未全，何嘗
translation_en:
…〔Yet in seeking one whose language and reasoning are both fully realized, I have found only this essay.〕
Examiner Zhang, School Director, comments: 〔It captures the substance of Cheng Tang’s cultivation of human relationships and expresses it thoroughly. This is an accomplished writer.〕
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: 〔All six matters concern Tang’s cultivation of himself. This essay correctly explains them throughout in terms of human relationships.〕

To fulfill the proper Way in each matter one undertakes: such was the former sage’s cultivation of human relationships. The former sage regarded human relationships as his personal responsibility; thus, in his work of cultivating them, he fulfilled the proper Way in each matter he undertook. A great minister cited this in admonishing a worthy king [?]. Was the loyal affection behind his purpose not profound? Formerly, Yi Yin wished Tai Jia to establish love and reverence and to take care at the outset. He therefore admonished him with these words, as if to say: “The former king Cheng Tang began by cultivating human relationships. How, indeed, can this be seen?

“Loyal counsel and forthright discussion sustain human relationships. Accordingly, he delighted tirelessly in goodness, following such counsel without resisting it. Worthy elders of established virtue provide leadership and examples in human relationships. Accordingly, whenever he saw goodness, he followed it, complying with their example without departing from it. When occupying a superior position, he personally practiced the Way of human relationships while governing, without the slightest indulgence, so that those below had something to observe and emulate. How well he was able to manifest clarity! When serving below, he expounded the Way of human relationships when offering admonition, without a moment’s deception, so that those above received warning and correction. How well he was able to fulfill his loyalty! When others were able to cultivate human relationships, he accepted whatever was good in them and did not reproach them for incompleteness in other virtues. When did he ever …

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
有求備之心乎在已雖能脩人紀也尤當察克
治惟恐有一善之未實曷嘗有自足之念哉湯
之所以脩人紀者如此太甲欲謹厥始可不知
所取法歟抑太甲以成湯之孫繼天下之大伊
尹懼其不能謹之於始故先曰罔不在初立愛
惟親立敬惟長故遂繼以成湯之所脩人紀者
以感動之蓋欲太甲立愛敬而謹厥始也噫伊
尹學堯舜者也堯舜之道孝弟而已觀其陳告
以此其有意致君為堯舜之君者歟
===
昔君文武丕平富不務咎底至齊信用昭
明於天下則亦有熊羆之士不二心之
臣保乂王家用端命于上帝皇天用訓
厥道付畀四方
楊浩
同考試官訓導陳　批　場中作者紛無定見
求體認真而發明透者無踰此篇宜錄出以式諸作
同考試官訓導曾　批　此題康王求助群臣
□□□□□□□□臣之助以見大業此篇傳釋之詳
punctuated:
有求備之心乎？在已雖能脩人紀也，尤當察克治，惟恐有一善之未實，曷嘗有自足之念哉！湯之所以脩人紀者如此，太甲欲謹厥始，可不知所取法歟？抑太甲以成湯之孫，繼天下之大，伊尹懼其不能謹之於始，故先曰：「罔不在初，立愛惟親，立敬惟長。」故遂繼以成湯之所脩人紀者以感動之，蓋欲太甲立愛敬而謹厥始也。噫！伊尹學堯舜者也，堯舜之道，孝弟而已。觀其陳告以此，其有意致君為堯舜之君者歟？

昔君文武丕平富，不務咎，底至齊，信用昭明於天下，則亦有熊羆之士、不二心之臣，保乂王家，用端命于上帝。皇天用訓厥道，付畀四方。

楊浩

同考試官訓導陳批：場中作者紛無定見，求體認真而發明透者，無踰此篇，宜錄出以式諸作。

同考試官訓導曾批：此題康王求助群臣，□□□□□□□□臣之助以見大業，此篇傳釋之詳
translation_en:
…ever entertained a desire to demand perfection? Although he himself could cultivate the norms of human relationships, he still had to scrutinize and discipline himself, fearing only that some good quality might not yet be fully realized. How could he ever have felt self-satisfied? Such was Tang’s cultivation of human relationships. If Tai Jia wished to exercise care at the beginning of his reign, could he fail to recognize whom he should take as his model? Moreover, Tai Jia, as Cheng Tang’s grandson, inherited the vast realm. Yi Yin feared that he might fail to exercise care at the outset, and therefore first said: “Everything depends upon the beginning. Establish love first toward one’s parents, and respect first toward one’s elders.” He then followed this with an account of Cheng Tang’s cultivation of human relationships, seeking to move him. His purpose was to have Tai Jia establish love and respect and exercise care at the beginning. Ah! Yi Yin was one who learned from Yao and Shun. The Way of Yao and Shun consists simply in filial devotion and fraternal respect. Considering that he offered these admonitions, did he not intend to make his ruler a sovereign like Yao and Shun?

“The former rulers, Wen and Wu, brought great peace and prosperity. They did not concentrate on finding fault, but brought about complete harmony, and their trustworthiness shone throughout the realm. They also had warriors fierce as bears and ministers of undivided loyalty, who protected and governed the royal house, thereby securing its mandate from the Lord on High. August Heaven accordingly approved their Way and entrusted the four quarters to them.”

Yang Hao.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, an Assistant Instructor: The candidates writing in the examination hall display a confusion of unsettled interpretations. For genuine understanding and penetrating exposition, no essay surpasses this one. It should be selected for inclusion as a model for other compositions.

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
矣作者多分撒不明殊庚本旨惟此篇作文足以明經旨
足以達意宜本房宜無忝
同考試官教諭劉　批　此篇本蔡傳作甚得
其旨視他卷不及也允宜錄出
考試官學正章　批　此題分截真包括盡
誠無忝此選
考試官教授鄭　批　此篇文理詳盡隱然
見康王求助群臣諸侯之意可取
前聖仁民之德而著於天下尤得群臣之輔以
===
胥辛天眷蓋臣之有益於君也尚矣前聖仁民
之德雖足以膺天眷能不資群臣以輔之哉宜
康王求助群臣諸侯而報誥之以此也想其意
若曰我周文武之為君以德不可不脩也刑罰
惟均平薄斂富民焉以罰不可不謹也則不務
咎惡輕省刑罰焉文武務德不務罰之心著於
外者推行而底其至存諸中者兼盡而極其誠
故光輝發越如日月之照臨光于四方民皆知
其尚德而不尚罰也顯于九有人皆知其務德
punctuated:
矣。作者多分撒不明，殊庚本旨，惟此篇作文足以明經旨，足以達意，宜本房宜無忝。
同考試官教諭劉批：此篇本蔡傳作，甚得其旨，視他卷不及也，允宜錄出。
考試官學正章批：此題分截真包括盡，誠無忝此選。
考試官教授鄭批：此篇文理詳盡，隱然見康王求助群臣諸侯之意，可取。
前聖仁民之德而著於天下，尤得群臣之輔以胥辛天眷。蓋臣之有益於君也尚矣。前聖仁民之德雖足以膺天眷，能不資群臣以輔之哉？宜康王求助群臣諸侯而報誥之以此也。想其意若曰：我周文武之為君，以德不可不脩也，刑罰惟均平，薄斂富民焉；以罰不可不謹也，則不務咎惡，輕省刑罰焉。文武務德不務罰之心，著於外者推行而底其至，存諸中者兼盡而極其誠。故光輝發越，如日月之照臨，光于四方，民皆知其尚德而不尚罰也；顯于九有，人皆知其務德
translation_en:
…[The preceding comment continues:] Most writers scatter their points without making them clear, departing from the original purport [?]. Only this essay adequately elucidates the Classic’s meaning and conveys its sense. It does credit to this examining section [?].
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: This essay follows Cai’s commentary and captures its meaning very well. Other scripts do not measure up to it. It certainly deserves to be selected for inclusion.
Examiner Zhang, Director of Studies, comments: The treatment of the topic’s divisions truly encompasses everything. It fully deserves this selection.
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: This essay’s reasoning is thorough and complete. It subtly brings out King Kang’s intention to seek assistance from his ministers and the feudal lords. It merits acceptance.
The former sage kings’ virtue in caring for the people became manifest throughout the world; above all, they obtained their ministers’ assistance in receiving Heaven’s favor [?]. Indeed, ministers have benefited their rulers since antiquity. Although the former sage kings’ virtue in caring for the people was sufficient to merit Heaven’s favor, could they dispense with their ministers’ assistance? It was fitting that King Kang, seeking aid from his ministers and the feudal lords, should address them in return with these words. We may imagine his meaning as follows: “When Wen and Wu of our Zhou ruled, they held that virtue must be cultivated: punishments were equitable [?], and they levied light taxes to enrich the people. Holding that punishments must be applied cautiously, they did not devote themselves to pursuing faults and wrongdoing, but mitigated and reduced penalties. Wen and Wu’s commitment to virtue rather than punishment, as expressed outwardly, was carried into practice to its fullest extent; as preserved within, it was fulfilled comprehensively and brought to the utmost sincerity. Thus their radiance shone forth like the illuminating sun and moon. It shone throughout the four quarters, and the people all knew that they esteemed virtue rather than punishment. It was manifest throughout the nine regions, and everyone knew that they devoted themselves to virtue…”

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
而不務咎也以文武之仁德遠著如此若無待
於群臣之輔矣求之當時則亦有熊羆武勇之
士戮力同心而翼衛乎王室不二心忠實之臣
并力效勞以保乂乎王家由是誕膺天命以撫
方夏我文王則有以受正命於上天矣簡畀殷
命尹爾多方我武王則有以受端命於上帝焉
然上帝不徒保佑命之而又於蒼蒼之表用順
其尚德不尚罰之道付之以輿圖之大而尺地
莫非其有也自天申之而又於冥冥之中用訓
===
其務德不務咎之心畀之以萬方之廣而一民
莫非其臣也文武得群臣之輔而膺天眷之隆
如此爾群臣諸侯可不輔導於我以紹於文武
乎抑觀康王以繼體守成之君而嗣文武重光
之運君臨之初舉此以告群臣諸侯意以文武
之聖尚得群臣之輔而獲乎天眷矧予小子爾
可不勉夫承弼厥辟之功哉厥後康王克盡君
道爲有周令主可謂有光於文武矣不然何以
曰不顯成康上帝是皇
punctuated:
而不務咎也。以文武之仁德遠著如此，若無待於群臣之輔矣。求之當時，則亦有熊羆武勇之士，戮力同心而翼衛乎王室；不二心忠實之臣，并力效勞以保乂乎王家。由是誕膺天命，以撫方夏，我文王則有以受正命於上天矣；簡畀殷命，尹爾多方，我武王則有以受端命於上帝焉。然上帝不徒保佑命之，而又於蒼蒼之表，用順其尚德不尚罰之道，付之以輿圖之大，而尺地莫非其有也；自天申之，而又於冥冥之中，用訓其務德不務咎之心，畀之以萬方之廣，而一民莫非其臣也。文武得群臣之輔，而膺天眷之隆如此，爾群臣諸侯可不輔導於我，以紹於文武乎？

抑觀康王，以繼體守成之君，而嗣文武重光之運，君臨之初，舉此以告群臣諸侯，意以文武之聖，尚得群臣之輔而獲乎天眷，矧予小子，爾可不勉夫承弼厥辟之功哉？厥後康王克盡君道，爲有周令主，可謂有光於文武矣。不然，何以曰：「不顯成康，上帝是皇」？
translation_en:
…and did not devote themselves to seeking out faults. With the benevolent virtue of Kings Wen and Wu so widely manifest, it might seem that they had no need of their ministers’ assistance. Yet, examining their times, we find warriors as valiant as bears, united in strength and purpose to protect the royal house, and loyal, steadfast ministers of undivided allegiance, combining their efforts in service to preserve and bring order to the royal household. Thus, grandly receiving Heaven’s Mandate and pacifying the central lands, our King Wen was able to receive the rightful Mandate from Heaven above. Chosen to receive the Mandate formerly held by Yin and to govern your many regions, our King Wu was able to receive the proper Mandate from the Lord on High. Yet the Lord on High did more than protect them and confer the Mandate upon them. Beyond the azure heavens, he accorded with their way of esteeming virtue rather than punishment, entrusting them with the vast territory of the realm, so that not a foot of land was outside their possession. Renewing this gift from Heaven, amid the unseen he guided their resolve to cultivate virtue rather than seek out faults, bestowing upon them the breadth of the myriad regions, so that not a single person was outside their rule. Such was the abundant favor of Heaven that Wen and Wu received through their ministers’ assistance. Can you ministers and regional lords fail to assist and guide me, so that I may carry on the work of Wen and Wu?

Now consider King Kang: as a ruler who inherited the throne and preserved its achievements, he succeeded to the doubly radiant legacy of Wen and Wu. At the outset of his reign, he invoked these matters in addressing his ministers and regional lords. His meaning was this: even sages such as Wen and Wu received their ministers’ assistance in securing Heaven’s favor; how much more must I, a young man, depend upon it! Can you fail to exert yourselves in supporting and assisting your sovereign? Thereafter, King Kang fully fulfilled the ruler’s way and became an excellent sovereign of Zhou. He may indeed be said to have added luster to Wen and Wu. Otherwise, why would it be said: “Were not Cheng and Kang illustrious? The Lord on High exalted them”?

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
詩
俾爾單厚何福不除
趙琮
同考試官訓導雷　批　〔塲中作者多以君之〕
〔富貴爲講令人厭觀此篇獨能融會傳義化腐〕
〔爲奇非深得葩經之旨者不能宜冠本房〕
考試官學正章　批　〔文理俱到優於衆作〕
〔健羨健羨〕
考試官教授鄭　批　〔善形容臣子祝君之〕
〔情且詞理俱到可取〕
===
詩人願天眷君以盡厚之福必其福之更新也
蓋福之更新乃所以盡厚也詩人以是祝君其
忠愛之意一何至哉昔人君以鹿鳴以下五詩
燕其臣臣受賜者歌此詩以答其君意謂吾君
以萬乘之尊居九重之上燕饗之際待臣之禮
至矣今我爲賓客我爲使臣將何以報之乎惟
願蒼蒼者天眷顧於冲漠之中使吾君獲福之
盡厚焉稱酬之頃優臣之意厚矣今我爲兄弟
punctuated:
詩
俾爾單厚，何福不除。
趙琮
同考試官訓導雷批：〔塲中作者多以君之〕〔富貴爲講，令人厭觀。此篇獨能融會傳義，化腐〕〔爲奇，非深得葩經之旨者不能，宜冠本房。〕
考試官學正章批：〔文理俱到，優於衆作。〕〔健羨，健羨！〕
考試官教授鄭批：〔善形容臣子祝君之〕〔情，且詞理俱到，可取。〕

詩人願天眷君以盡厚之福，必其福之更新也。蓋福之更新，乃所以盡厚也。詩人以是祝君，其忠愛之意一何至哉！昔人君以《鹿鳴》以下五詩燕其臣，臣受賜者歌此詩以答其君，意謂：吾君以萬乘之尊，居九重之上，燕饗之際，待臣之禮至矣。今我爲賓客，我爲使臣，將何以報之乎？惟願蒼蒼者天眷顧於冲漠之中，使吾君獲福之盡厚焉。稱酬之頃，優臣之意厚矣。今我爲兄弟，
translation_en:
Book of Odes
“May you be blessed with utter abundance; what blessing will not be renewed?”
Zhao Cong

Comment by Associate Examiner Lei, an Assistant Instructor: “Most writers in the examination hall expound upon the ruler’s wealth and rank, making their essays tiresome to read. This essay alone integrates the meanings of the commentaries and transforms the stale into the remarkable. Only someone who has deeply grasped the purport of the Book of Odes could accomplish this. It should rank first in this examination section.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, an Instructor: “Both the writing and the reasoning are fully realized, surpassing the other compositions. Admirable, admirable!”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, a Professor: “It aptly conveys the feelings of a subject praying for his ruler’s blessings. Moreover, both its expression and its reasoning are fully realized. It merits selection.”

The poet wishes Heaven to favor the ruler with blessings of the fullest abundance; this necessarily entails the renewal of those blessings. For it is through renewal that blessings attain their fullest abundance. With these words the poet prays for his ruler: how profound his loyalty and love!

In antiquity, the ruler entertained his subjects with the five odes beginning with “The Deer Call” (Lu ming). The subjects who received his bounty sang this ode in response to their ruler. Their meaning was: Our ruler, with the dignity of a sovereign of ten thousand chariots, dwells above the ninefold palace gates. At the banquet, the ritual courtesy with which he treats his subjects is consummate. Now, as a guest, as an envoy, how shall I repay him? I can only wish that azure Heaven, from within its still and formless realm, would look upon him with favor and grant our ruler blessings of the fullest abundance. As the toasts are exchanged, his intention to honor his subjects is most generous. Now, as a brother …

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
我為朋友將何以答之乎惟願皇皇后帝保佑
於穹窿之表俾吾君獲福之單厚焉然福之單
厚果何如哉彼舊者除而新者不生非單厚也
願吾君之福舊者既除而新者又生初無窮巳
其單厚也為何如往者消而來者不續非盡厚
也願吾君之福往者方消而來者復續初無間
斷其盡厚也又何如噫臣子答君之賜者其忠
愛之誠有如是夫抑嘗論之君臣之分以嚴為
主朝廷之禮以敬為主然一於嚴敬則情或不
通有周王者制為燕饗之禮以通上下之情君
以恩禮施之臣以祝願報之此盛時君臣所以
上下交而德業成也猗歟盛哉
王鼇爾成來咨來茹嗟嗟保介維莫之春
亦又何求如何新畬於皇來牟將受厥
明明昭上帝迄用康年命我衆人庤乃
錢鎛奄觀銍艾
===
同考試官訓導雷　批　場中作此題者互有
趙琮
punctuated:
我為朋友，將何以答之乎？惟願皇皇后帝保佑於穹窿之表，俾吾君獲福之單厚焉。然福之單厚果何如哉？彼舊者除而新者不生，非單厚也。願吾君之福，舊者既除而新者又生，初無窮巳，其單厚也為何如？往者消而來者不續，非盡厚也。願吾君之福，往者方消而來者復續，初無間斷，其盡厚也又何如？噫！臣子答君之賜者，其忠愛之誠有如是夫！抑嘗論之：君臣之分以嚴為主，朝廷之禮以敬為主。然一於嚴敬，則情或不通。有周王者制為燕饗之禮，以通上下之情。君以恩禮施之，臣以祝願報之，此盛時君臣所以上下交而德業成也。猗歟，盛哉！
王鼇爾成，來咨來茹。嗟嗟保介，維莫之春，亦又何求？如何新畬？於皇來牟，將受厥明。明昭上帝，迄用康年。命我衆人：庤乃錢鎛，奄觀銍艾。
同考試官訓導雷批：場中作此題者，互有
趙琮
translation_en:
…I stand as a friend: how shall I respond? I wish only that the august Sovereign on High would grant protection from beyond the vault of heaven, enabling our ruler to receive blessings in their fullest abundance. But what is this fullness of blessing? If old blessings pass away and new ones do not arise, that is no fullness. May our ruler’s blessings be such that, when old ones have passed away, new ones arise, without ever reaching an end. How abundant such blessings would be! If past blessings fade and those to come do not continue them, that is no complete abundance. May our ruler’s blessings be such that, just as past ones fade, those to come succeed them, without any interruption. How complete such abundance would be! Ah! Such is the sincerity of the loyal affection with which a minister responds to his ruler’s gifts!
Yet I have reflected on this: the distinction between ruler and minister rests chiefly on strictness, and court ritual rests chiefly on reverence. But if strictness and reverence alone prevail, feelings may fail to find expression. The kings of Zhou instituted the rites of feasting to allow feelings to pass between those above and those below. The ruler bestowed kindness and ceremonial honors; his ministers repaid him with good wishes. This is how, in that flourishing age, ruler and ministers communicated across their respective stations and brought their virtuous achievements to completion. Ah, how splendid!
The king grants you success [?]; come to consult and deliberate. Ah, agricultural officers, it is now late spring: what further matters require attention? How fare the newly reclaimed fields and those in their third year? Ah, the splendid wheat and barley! They are about to receive their ripening bounty. The brightly manifest Lord on High will finally grant a bountiful year. Command our people: prepare your spades and hoes; soon we shall see the sickles reaping.

Zhao Cong.

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
得失純正者無如此篇中間戒命之詞和而不迫真
高作也
考試官學正章　批　周王戒命農官之意
文足以發之
考試官教授鄭　批　詞簡意明蓋熟於
本領者
以成法當求而復詳言其事其重農之意爲何
夫豐穰係農官之勤惰所當戒命也周王既戒
王者戒農官以求成法必戒其副而詳其事也
===
如哉此戒農官之詩其意蓋謂我周之先以稼
穡教民以農事開國春耕夏耘莫不有一定之
成法爾臣工所宜知也今我勑爾以成法爾當
夙夜在公是究是圖可焉于耜舉趾莫不有一
定之成憲爾臣工所宜度也今我釐爾以成憲
爾當夙夜匪懈來咨來度可焉然成法固所當
求苟不示以所戒之事孰知何所求哉於是又
謂嗟爾保介職副農官當莫春之月乃治田之
時斯時也果何求哉亦惟治其新畬之田耳今
punctuated:
得失，純正者無如此篇，中間戒命之詞，和而不迫，真高作也。

考試官學正章，批：周王戒命農官之意，文足以發之。

考試官教授鄭，批：詞簡意明，蓋熟於本領者。

以成法當求，而復詳言其事，其重農之意爲何？夫豐穰係農官之勤惰，所當戒命也。周王既戒，王者戒農官以求成法，必戒其副而詳其事也。如哉？此戒農官之詩，其意蓋謂：我周之先，以稼穡教民，以農事開國。春耕夏耘，莫不有一定之成法，爾臣工所宜知也。今我勑爾以成法，爾當夙夜在公，是究是圖可焉。于耜舉趾，莫不有一定之成憲，爾臣工所宜度也。今我釐爾以成憲，爾當夙夜匪懈，來咨來度可焉。然成法固所當求，苟不示以所戒之事，孰知何所求哉？於是又謂：嗟爾保介，職副農官，當莫春之月，乃治田之時。斯時也，果何求哉？亦惟治其新畬之田耳。今
translation_en:
…have their strengths and weaknesses, but none equals this piece in purity and correctness. Its words of admonition and instruction are harmonious without being overbearing: truly an outstanding composition.

Examiner Zhang, an instructor, comments: “This essay fully brings out the intention behind the Zhou king’s admonitions and instructions to his agricultural officials.”

Examiner Zheng, a professor, comments: “The language is concise and the meaning clear; the writer evidently has a firm grasp of the fundamentals.”

“Established methods should be sought,” yet he goes on to explain the tasks in detail: what does this reveal about his concern for agriculture? Abundant harvests depend on the diligence or indolence of agricultural officials, who must therefore be admonished and instructed. The Zhou king, having already admonished them—when a king admonishes agricultural officials to seek established methods, he must also admonish their deputies and explain their tasks in detail. How so? [The transcribed clauses here appear to be out of order; their connections are uncertain.]

This poem admonishing agricultural officials means, in substance: “Our Zhou ancestors taught the people to sow and reap, and founded the state upon agriculture. For spring plowing and summer weeding alike, there are fixed, established methods, which you, my officials, ought to know. Now that I instruct you in these established methods, you should attend to public duties morning and night, examining and considering them. For preparing the plowshares and setting out to work, there are likewise fixed, established rules, which you, my officials, ought to consider. Now that I direct you according to these established rules, you should be unremitting morning and night, coming to consult and deliberate.”

Yet although established methods must indeed be sought, unless the tasks to which the admonitions pertain are made clear, who will know what to seek? Thus he says further: “Ah, you assistant agricultural officials, whose duty is to serve as deputies to the agricultural officials! It is the last month of spring, the season for tending the fields. At this time, what indeed should you seek? Only to tend your fields in their second and third years of cultivation. Now…”

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
畬新畬抑何如哉然而麥已將熟則可以受上
帝之明賜矣夫來牟可必嘉穀之占而此明昭
之上帝又將賜我新畬以豐年也農官於此宜
如之何但命我甸徒庤乃錢鎛以致力於新田
而銍艾之舉特奄忽之間爾具我農器以致力
於畬田而收成之候特頃刻之際爾豈可以為
久而難待而懈於用力也哉周王於農官而戒
飭之如此可謂不忘所自矣抑嘗考之有周之
興后稷教民稼穡公劉克篤民事文王之卽田
===
功武王之重民食歷世相承皆以農事為重也
成王繼之又拳拳焉以戒飭農官可謂能盡繼
述之道者矣噫蒼姬永建八百餘年良有以夫
春秋
城楚丘〔僖公二年〕諸侯城緣陵〔僖公十四年〕蔡侯
廬歸于蔡陳侯吳歸于陳〔昭公十三年〕
鮑壤
考試官學正章　批
楚丘緣陵學者雖知抑齊楚之封而不知存恤患之功深繼絕之迹此篇得之是
punctuated:
畬新畬，抑何如哉？然而麥已將熟，則可以受上帝之明賜矣。夫來牟可必嘉穀之占，而此明昭之上帝又將賜我新畬以豐年也。農官於此宜如之何？但命我甸徒庤乃錢鎛，以致力於新田，而銍艾之舉特奄忽之間爾；具我農器，以致力於畬田，而收成之候特頃刻之際爾。豈可以為久而難待，而懈於用力也哉？周王於農官而戒飭之如此，可謂不忘所自矣。抑嘗考之，有周之興，后稷教民稼穡，公劉克篤民事，文王之卽田功，武王之重民食，歷世相承，皆以農事為重也。成王繼之，又拳拳焉以戒飭農官，可謂能盡繼述之道者矣。噫！蒼姬永建八百餘年，良有以夫！

春秋
「城楚丘。」〔僖公二年〕「諸侯城緣陵。」〔僖公十四年〕「蔡侯廬歸于蔡，陳侯吳歸于陳。」〔昭公十三年〕
鮑壤

考試官學正章，批：
楚丘、緣陵，學者雖知抑齊楚之封，而不知存恤患之功、深繼絕之迹。此篇得之，是
translation_en:
…the reclaimed and newly cultivated fields—how do they stand [?]? Yet the wheat is already nearly ripe, and so we may receive the manifest bounty of the Lord on High. Wheat and barley provide a sure indication of a fine grain harvest, and this radiant Lord on High will also grant our newly cultivated and reclaimed fields an abundant year. What, then, should the agricultural officials do? Simply order our field laborers to prepare their spades and hoes and devote their efforts to the new fields: reaping with sickles will come in no more than an instant. Equip them with our agricultural implements to work the reclaimed fields: harvest time will arrive in but a moment. How could they suppose it so distant and difficult to await that they slacken their efforts? In admonishing the agricultural officials in this way, the king of Zhou may truly be said not to have forgotten the source of his inheritance.

I have considered the rise of Zhou: Hou Ji taught the people to sow and reap; Gong Liu devoted himself earnestly to the people's affairs; King Wen applied himself to agricultural work; and King Wu attached great importance to the people's food. Through successive generations, all treated agriculture as a matter of great importance. King Cheng succeeded them and likewise admonished the agricultural officials with earnest concern. He may be said to have fully fulfilled the duty of carrying forward his predecessors' work. Ah! There was indeed good reason why the Ji house of Zhou remained established for more than eight hundred years!

Bao Rang
