title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
窗錄出
考試官教授鄭　批　齊桓楚平封衛杞蔡
陳之書法是篇發之殆無餘蘊
春秋抑伯主專封而猶存其恤患之功抑外夷
專封而必泯其繼絕之迹此楚丘緣陵之城所
以不書衛杞而蔡廬陳吳之歸所以不書自楚
也聖人之意何如哉昔衛為狄患杞為夷患二
國嘗淪於危亡矣齊桓主伯責任安攘始率會
糧諸侯城楚丘以存衛繼率會鹹諸侯城緣陵
===
以遷杞築斯城也為之藩籬鑿斯池也為之屏
障雖曰為利於衛為甚博有功於杞為甚大然
而黼扆不設於王朝策命不作於內史齊桓是
舉語功利則高矣語道義則三王之罪人也春
秋於此欲詳書歟其罪不彰不可也欲書衛杞
歟其功不著不可也故書城楚丘城緣陵而不
書衛杞者豈非抑伯主專封而猶存其恤患之
功乎至若陳滅於楚蔡滅於楚二國已底於危
亡矣棄疾即位欲矯靈惡始以隱太子有之子
punctuated:
窗錄出。
考試官教授鄭批：齊桓、楚平封衛、杞、蔡、陳之書法，是篇發之殆無餘蘊。
春秋抑伯主專封，而猶存其恤患之功；抑外夷專封，而必泯其繼絕之迹。此楚丘、緣陵之城所以不書衛、杞，而蔡廬、陳吳之歸所以不書自楚也。聖人之意何如哉？昔衛為狄患，杞為夷患，二國嘗淪於危亡矣。齊桓主伯，責任安攘，始率會糧諸侯城楚丘以存衛，繼率會鹹諸侯城緣陵以遷杞。築斯城也，為之藩籬；鑿斯池也，為之屏障。雖曰為利於衛為甚博，有功於杞為甚大，然而黼扆不設於王朝，策命不作於內史。齊桓是舉，語功利則高矣，語道義則三王之罪人也。春秋於此，欲詳書歟？其罪不彰，不可也。欲書衛、杞歟？其功不著，不可也。故書城楚丘、城緣陵而不書衛、杞者，豈非抑伯主專封而猶存其恤患之功乎？至若陳滅於楚，蔡滅於楚，二國已底於危亡矣。棄疾即位，欲矯靈惡，始以隱太子有之子
translation_en:
…selected for inclusion from the examination hall [?].

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Professor: This essay elucidates almost exhaustively the principles governing how the enfeoffments of Wei, Qi 杞, Cai, and Chen by Duke Huan of Qi 齊 and King Ping of Chu are recorded.

The Spring and Autumn Annals censures the hegemon’s unauthorized enfeoffments, yet preserves recognition of his achievement in relieving distress; it censures unauthorized enfeoffments by an outer barbarian ruler and necessarily effaces the traces of his restoration of extinguished ruling lines. This is why the walling of Chuqiu and Yuanling is recorded without naming Wei and Qi, and why the returns of Lu of Cai and Wu of Chen are recorded without saying “from Chu.” What was the Sage’s intent?

Formerly, Wei suffered attacks by the Di and Qi suffered attacks by the Yi; both states had fallen into mortal peril. Duke Huan of Qi held the hegemony and bore responsibility for securing the states and repelling outsiders. First, he led the feudal lords assembled at Liang [?] to wall Chuqiu and preserve Wei; subsequently, he led the feudal lords assembled at Xian to wall Yuanling and relocate Qi there. Building these walls provided them with a protective fence; digging these moats provided them with a defensive barrier. Although the benefits bestowed on Wei were very extensive and the service rendered to Qi very great, no embroidered ceremonial screen was set up at the royal court, nor was an investiture mandate prepared by the Interior Scribe. Judged by its achievements and benefits, this undertaking of Duke Huan was lofty indeed; judged by the Way and righteousness, however, it made him an offender against the Three Kings.

Should the Spring and Autumn Annals have recorded these events in detail? His offense would not have been made manifest: that would not do. Should it have named Wei and Qi? His achievement would not have been evident: that would not do. Thus it records the walling of Chuqiu and Yuanling without naming Wei and Qi. Does this not censure the hegemon’s unauthorized enfeoffments while preserving recognition of his achievement in relieving distress?

As for Chen and Cai, both had been extinguished by Chu, and both states had already reached the point of destruction. When Qiji ascended the throne, he wished to redress King Ling’s wickedness. First, he took the son of You, the posthumously titled Crown Prince Yin …

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
盧歸于蔡繼以悼太子偃師之子吳歸于陳土
地人民悉以與之儀章器物悉以歸之雖曰悔
過遷善興滅繼絕然以五等之君非外夷所得
制諸夏之國亦非外夷所得封楚平是舉論其
事可恕矣論其心寔中國之罪人也春秋於此
欲稱復歸歟是與楚之滅不可也欲言自楚歟
是與楚之封不可也此書蔡盧陳吳歸其國而
不言自楚者又非抑外夷專封而必泯其繼絕
之迹乎吁因一專封也恤患也在齊則待之恕
===
在楚則待之嚴其內夏外夷之意可見矣攷之
先王之世嘗聞荆狄來王來威也傳至後世繼
狄繼楚先後橫行中國而莫之顧伊誰之責歟
噫世道一變而為伯再變而為吳楚又變而為
戰國春秋為王道計世道計中國計不得不謹
嚴於書法也非孔子莫能脩於斯尤信
公會晉侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衛子莒子
盟于踐土〔僖公二十八年晉侯伐衛文公元年同〕
盟于亳城北〔襄公十一年仲孫羯會晉荀盈〕
punctuated:
盧歸于蔡，繼以悼太子偃師之子吳歸于陳，土地人民悉以與之，儀章器物悉以歸之。雖曰悔過遷善，興滅繼絕，然以五等之君，非外夷所得制；諸夏之國，亦非外夷所得封。楚平是舉，論其事可恕矣，論其心，寔中國之罪人也。《春秋》於此，欲稱復歸歟？是與楚之滅，不可也。欲言自楚歟？是與楚之封，不可也。此書蔡盧、陳吳歸其國而不言自楚者，又非抑外夷專封而必泯其繼絕之迹乎？吁！因一專封也，恤患也，在齊則待之恕，在楚則待之嚴，其內夏外夷之意可見矣。攷之先王之世，嘗聞荆狄來王來威也。傳至後世，繼狄繼楚，先後橫行中國而莫之顧，伊誰之責歟？噫！世道一變而為伯，再變而為吳楚，又變而為戰國。《春秋》為王道計、世道計、中國計，不得不謹嚴於書法也。「非孔子莫能脩」，於斯尤信。
公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衛子、莒子。
盟于踐土。〔僖公二十八年，晉侯伐衛，文公元年同。〕
盟于亳城北。〔襄公十一年，仲孫羯會晉荀盈〕
translation_en:
…Lu to return to Cai, and then had Wu, the son of Crown Prince Dao, Yanshi, return to Chen. He gave them all their lands and people and restored all their ceremonial insignia and vessels. Although this might be called repenting of wrongdoing and turning toward goodness, reviving extinguished states and continuing severed lines of succession, rulers of the five noble ranks were not subject to the control of an outer barbarian power; nor could such a power invest rulers of the states of the Xia. In this undertaking by King Ping of Chu, his deeds might be excused, but judged by his intentions, he was truly an offender against the Central States. How should the Spring and Autumn Annals record this? Should it say “returned again”? That would sanction Chu’s destruction of those states, which would not do. Should it say “from Chu”? That would sanction Chu’s investiture of their rulers, which would not do. Thus it records Lu of Cai and Wu of Chen returning to their states without saying “from Chu.” Does this not likewise condemn an outer barbarian power’s unauthorized investitures, while deliberately effacing any trace of its restoration of severed lines of succession? Ah! In the same matters of unauthorized investiture and relief of distress, Qi is treated leniently, but Chu strictly. Here we can see the intent to treat the Xia as insiders and the barbarians as outsiders.
Looking back to the age of the former kings, we have heard that Jing and the Di came to acknowledge royal authority and submit to its majesty. In later ages, the Di and Chu in succession [?] ran rampant through the Central States, and no one paid heed. Whose responsibility was this? Alas! With one transformation, the order of the world became that of the hegemons; with another, that of Wu and Chu; with yet another, that of the Warring States. For the sake of the Way of Kings, the order of the world, and the Central States, the Spring and Autumn Annals could not but be exacting and strict in its manner of recording events. The saying “None but Confucius could have compiled it” is especially borne out here.
The duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju.
They concluded a covenant at Jiantu. 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi. “The Marquis of Jin attacked Wei,” in the first year of Duke Wen, is treated together with this [?].〕
They concluded a covenant north of the city of Bo. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xiang. Zhongsun Jie met with Xun Ying of Jin…〕

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
齊高止宋華定衛世叔儀鄭公孫段曹
人莒人滕人薛人小邾人城杞〔襄公二十九年〕
鮑瑾
考試官學正章　批　此題作者多不知裁
〔衛盟萬邑城北為襄悼尊王事間有知者又欠發揮簡〕
〔明可觀獨有是作政錄以示學者〕
考試官教授鄭　批　詞簡理當迥異衆作
人之業不可不脩也晉平不能脩文襄悼公之
緒業成于前而隳于後春秋深致其意焉蓋先
===
業而徒為私親之計春秋得不備書以致其意
哉昔晉文自歸國以來一戰勝楚遂主夏盟於
是荷天王下勞盟踐土以著尊王之義更敵讎
衛侯不朝于温以達臣下之情已而悼公為
𡒄城北之盟而申尊獎王室之約脩禮于父
子昭信義于後先西周之好音再續中國之風
采一新若三公者可謂能盡厥職而成伯業矣
以至平公繼悼使能繩其祖武則前人之業于
焉不墜前人之績于焉不泯夫何不此之圖乃
punctuated:
齊高止、宋華定、衛世叔儀、鄭公孫段、曹人、莒人、滕人、薛人、小邾人城杞。〔襄公二十九年〕
鮑瑾。
考試官學正章批：此題作者多不知裁。〔衛盟萬邑城北為襄悼尊王事，間有知者，又欠發揮，簡〕〔明可觀，獨有是作，政錄以示學者。〕
考試官教授鄭批：詞簡理當，迥異衆作。
人之業不可不脩也。晉平不能脩文、襄、悼公之緒，業成于前而隳于後，《春秋》深致其意焉。蓋先業而徒為私親之計，《春秋》得不備書以致其意哉？昔晉文自歸國以來，一戰勝楚，遂主夏盟。於是荷天王下勞，盟踐土以著尊王之義；更敵讎衛侯不朝于温，以達臣下之情。已而悼公為𡒄城北之盟，而申尊獎王室之約。脩禮于父子，昭信義于後先，西周之好音再續，中國之風采一新。若三公者，可謂能盡厥職而成伯業矣。以至平公繼悼，使能繩其祖武，則前人之業于焉不墜，前人之績于焉不泯。夫何不此之圖，乃
translation_en:
…Gao Zhi of Qi, Hua Ding of Song, Shishu Yi of Wei, Gongsun Duan of Zheng, and men of Cao, Ju, Teng, Xue, and Little Zhu fortified Qi. 〔The twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang.〕
Bao Jin.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, School Instructor: Most who wrote on this topic did not know how to organize their material. 〔The passages concerning Wei, the covenant, Wan, and the north of the city [?] concern Dukes Xiang and Dao honoring the king. Even those who understood this failed to develop it adequately. This composition alone is concise, clear, and worth reading; it is duly recorded [?] to show students.〕
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Professor: The language is concise and the reasoning sound, markedly different from the other compositions.
A man’s accomplishments must be maintained. Duke Ping of Jin could not carry forward the legacy of Dukes Wen, Xiang, and Dao: achievements established earlier were subsequently ruined. The Spring and Autumn Annals conveys its meaning profoundly here. As for the inherited achievements [?], he merely schemed for the benefit of his own relatives. How could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to record the matter fully to convey its meaning?
Formerly, after Duke Wen of Jin returned to his state, he defeated Chu in a single battle and consequently presided over the covenants of the Chinese states. He then received the honor of the Heavenly King coming down to commend him, and concluded the covenant at Jiantu to make manifest the principle of honoring the king. Further, concerning his enemy, the Marquis of Wei, who did not attend court at Wen [?], he conveyed the sentiments of a subject. Later, Duke Dao concluded the covenant north of the city of [Bo?], reaffirming the pledge to honor and support the royal house. Ritual propriety was cultivated between fathers and sons, and trustworthiness and righteousness were made manifest among predecessors and successors. The fine strains of Western Zhou sounded once more, and the Chinese states acquired a renewed splendor. Such men as these three dukes may be said to have fully discharged their duties and established the achievements of a hegemon.
When Duke Ping succeeded Duke Dao, had he been able to follow in his ancestors’ footsteps, his predecessors’ enterprise would thereby have been preserved and their achievements would not have been effaced. Why did he fail to pursue this, and instead…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
命列國之臣為城杞之舉不恤宗周之闕而夏
肄是屏本末倒置也輕棄諸姬之國而毋家是
親輕重失倫也書曰若考作室厥子弗肯堂厥父
菑厥子弗肯播其平公之謂歟春秋於三公書
侯晉同盟蓋予之也城杞大夫稱名稱人蓋貶
之也聖人之意為何如吁勤于尊王者公也必
褒之暱于毋族者私也必貶之春秋之法其嚴
乎雖然平公之庸固無容議文公因天王下勞
始為踐土之盟襄公因伐衛興師始有于溫之
覲悼公因伐鄭同盟始講辨王之信假此欺人
實欲遂己私耳故曰有伯非美事不可不知
禮記
太傅在前少傅在後入則有保出則有師
是以教喻而德成也
趙珩
同考試官訓導左　批〔此題本易作者多求德成處只明性此作得之是用錄出〕
考試官學正章　批〔理明詞切殊勝他卷〕
punctuated:
命列國之臣為城杞之舉，不恤宗周之闕，而夏肄是屏，本末倒置也；輕棄諸姬之國，而毋家是親，輕重失倫也。《書》曰：「若考作室，厥子弗肯堂；厥父菑，厥子弗肯播。」其平公之謂歟？《春秋》於三公書「侯晉同盟」，蓋予之也；城杞大夫稱名、稱人，蓋貶之也。聖人之意為何如？吁！勤于尊王者，公也，必褒之；暱于毋族者，私也，必貶之。《春秋》之法，其嚴乎！雖然，平公之庸固無容議，文公因天王下勞，始為踐土之盟；襄公因伐衛興師，始有于溫之覲；悼公因伐鄭同盟，始講辨王之信。假此欺人，實欲遂己私耳。故曰：「有伯非美事。」不可不知。

《禮記》
太傅在前，少傅在後，入則有保，出則有師，是以教喻而德成也。

趙珩

同考試官訓導左　批〔此題本易，作者多求德成處，只明性，此作得之，是用錄出。〕
考試官學正章　批〔理明詞切，殊勝他卷。〕
translation_en:
…ordered the ministers of the various states to undertake the fortification of Qi. He took no account of the deficiencies of the Zhou royal house, but protected the descendants of Xia: this inverted root and branch. He lightly cast aside the states of the Ji lineage, but favored his mother's family [?]: this confused the relative importance of things. The Book of Documents says: “If a father builds a house, his son refuses to complete its hall; if his father clears the land, his son refuses to sow it.” Does this not describe Duke Ping? In its entries concerning the three dukes, the Spring and Autumn Annals records “the lords and Jin entered a covenant together” [?], thereby approving them. In recording the fortification of Qi, it designates the grand masters by their personal names or merely as “men,” thereby censuring them. What was the sage's intention? Ah! Diligence in honoring the king serves the public good and must be praised; favoritism toward one's maternal clan [?] serves private interests and must be censured. How stern are the standards of the Spring and Autumn Annals!

Nevertheless, although Duke Ping's mediocrity is beyond dispute, Duke Wen concluded the covenant at Jiantu only because the Son of Heaven came down to reward his exertions; Duke Xiang held the audience at Wen only because troops had been raised to attack Wei; and Duke Dao began to affirm his pledge to serve the king [?] only because an alliance had been formed to attack Zheng. They used these occasions to deceive others, while in truth seeking only to fulfill their own private desires. Thus it is said: “The existence of hegemons is no fine thing.” This must be understood.

Book of Rites

“The Grand Mentor is in front and the Junior Mentor behind; within, there is a Guardian, and outside, there is a Preceptor. Thus instruction is understood and virtue is perfected.”

Zhao Heng

Comment by Associate Examiner Zuo, Assistant Instructor: 〔This topic is fundamentally easy. Most writers seek to address the point about perfecting virtue, but merely explain human nature [?]. This essay grasps it, and for that reason it has been selected for inclusion.〕

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔The principles are clearly explained and the wording is apt; it is decidedly superior to the other papers.〕

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授鄭　批　〔備出三王教世子之意優於他作〕
先王之教世子也惟隨寓有其人故教明而德
備蓋世子之所以教明而德備者由乎輔導之
有人也使輔導之其人則教且不喻又何以成
其德哉今夫世子君之儲貳國之根本故三王
既以禮樂而教之必立太傅少傅師保以養之
焉養之何如以言其行步也太傅則在於前示
世子以父子君臣之道少傅則在於後奉世子
===
以觀太傅之行一前一後而皆有所養焉以審
其居處也入焉有保輔其身而歸諸道出焉有
師教以事而喻諸德一出一入而咸有所養焉
夫惟前後出入皆有所養是以薰陶之久而心
與理融漸染之深而身與道合向於父子之教
有未喻也今則曉然知父之當慈子之當孝而
慈孝之德成諸己者粹然一中和之著向於君
臣之教有未喻也今則洞然知君之當仁臣之
當忠而仁忠之德萃諸躬者渾然無駁雜之□
punctuated:
考試官教授鄭，批：〔備出三王教世子之意，優於他作。〕

先王之教世子也，惟隨寓有其人，故教明而德備。蓋世子之所以教明而德備者，由乎輔導之有人也。使輔導之其人，則教且不喻，又何以成其德哉？今夫世子，君之儲貳，國之根本。故三王既以禮樂而教之，必立太傅、少傅、師保以養之焉。養之何如？以言其行步也，太傅則在於前，示世子以父子君臣之道；少傅則在於後，奉世子以觀太傅之行。一前一後，而皆有所養焉。以審其居處也，入焉有保，輔其身而歸諸道；出焉有師，教以事而喻諸德。一出一入，而咸有所養焉。夫惟前後出入皆有所養，是以薰陶之久而心與理融，漸染之深而身與道合。向於父子之教有未喻也，今則曉然知父之當慈、子之當孝，而慈孝之德成諸己者，粹然一中和之著；向於君臣之教有未喻也，今則洞然知君之當仁、臣之當忠，而仁忠之德萃諸躬者，渾然無駁雜之□
translation_en:
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: 〔Fully brings out the intentions of the Three Kings in educating the heir apparent; superior to the other compositions.〕

When the former kings educated the heir apparent, suitable men attended him wherever he was; thus he understood his instruction and became complete in virtue. Indeed, his understanding of instruction and completeness in virtue depended on having men to assist and guide him. If those guiding him were [not?] suitable men, he would not even understand his instruction; how, then, could his virtue be perfected?

Now, the heir apparent is the ruler’s designated successor and the foundation of the state. Thus, besides teaching him through rites and music, the Three Kings invariably appointed a Grand Mentor, a Junior Mentor, a Preceptor, and a Guardian to nurture him. How did they nurture him? When he walked, the Grand Mentor went before him, demonstrating the Way governing fathers and sons, rulers and ministers; the Junior Mentor followed behind, attending the heir apparent as he observed the Grand Mentor’s conduct. With one before and one behind, there was always someone to nurture him. Considering his daily life, when he entered, a Guardian assisted him personally and brought him into accord with the Way; when he went out, a Preceptor instructed him in affairs and brought him to understand virtue. Whether going out or coming in, he was always nurtured.

Since he received this nurture before and behind, going out and coming in, prolonged cultivation brought his mind into harmony with principle, while its deeply permeating influence brought his person into accord with the Way. Previously, there had been things he did not understand in the teaching concerning fathers and sons; now he clearly knew that a father should be loving and a son filial. The virtues of parental love and filial devotion, perfected within himself, became a pure manifestation of equilibrium and harmony. Previously, there had been things he did not understand in the teaching concerning rulers and ministers; now he thoroughly knew that a ruler should be benevolent and a minister loyal. The virtues of benevolence and loyalty, gathered within his person, formed an integral whole free from admixture of [illegible] …

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
世子教喻而德成如此此其所以克紹洪業而
保有天下之大也歟抑論三王之教世子禮以
脩其外樂以脩其內其道備矣苟非教之之人
則道不能以自行是以又立太傅少傅師保之
官養之以成其德也及其德成則又有以致夫
教尊而官正官正而國治矣語曰樂正司業父
師司成一有元良萬國以貞誼不信夫
義生然後禮作禮作然後萬物安
趙珩
===

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
別而後父子親子親其父必推父所自出而上
親於祖以至於高祖父親其子必推子之所生
而下親於孫以及於玄孫或親或疏處之而各
得其宜或遠或近施之而咸得其當則義之生
也為何如義既生矣故自父而祖自祖以至於
高祖各隨其恩之隆殺而著其節文自子而孫
自孫以至於玄孫各循其情之戚疏而為之品
節見於日用之間粲然而有文形於彝倫之際
秩然而有序則禮之作也為何若禮既作矣故
===
上自父祖以及從父從祖莫不由是而各得其
所下自子孫以及從子從孫罔不因之而各安
其位則萬物之安也又何如哉吁義生而禮作
禮作而物安一由於男女有別而起然則大昏
之禮迎得不敬摯相見以敬章別乎大抵昏禮
萬世之始人道之原也是以聖王重之而著其
禮執摯而後相見敬重而後相親皆所以成男
女之別而立夫婦之義也然豈惟禮重之而已
易首乾坤而重咸恒詩首關雎而戒淫泆亦所

translation_en: …only after there is distinction between men and women is there affection between father and son. A son who loves his father must extend that affection upward to those from whom his father sprang—to his grandfather and as far as his great-great-grandfather. A father who loves his son must extend that affection downward to his son’s offspring—to his grandson and as far as his great-great-grandson. Whether kinship is close or distant, each is treated as is fitting; whether the relationship is remote or near, what is accorded to each is appropriate. How, then, does righteousness arise? Once righteousness has arisen, patterned observances are established for each ascending generation, from father to grandfather and onward to great-great-grandfather, according to the greater or lesser degree of affection owed to each. For each descending generation, from son to grandson and onward to great-great-grandson, graded observances are likewise instituted according to the closeness or remoteness of feeling. Manifested in daily life, these observances display a splendid pattern; expressed in the enduring human relationships, they exhibit orderly arrangement. How, then, does ritual take shape? Once ritual has taken shape, all above, from fathers and grandfathers to paternal uncles and granduncles, thereby obtain their proper places; all below, from sons and grandsons to nephews and grandnephews, thereby rest secure in their respective positions. How, then, do all things attain repose? Ah! Righteousness arises and ritual takes shape; ritual takes shape and things find repose. All this originates in the distinction between men and women. Thus, in the great marriage rite, could the welcoming and the presentation of gifts at the meeting fail to be reverent, using reverence to manifest distinction [?]? title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:

大生民之衆饑者欲食吾不能推父母之
心以食之弗愛也寒者欲衣吾不能推父
母之心以衣之弗愛也老者欲安少者欲
懷勞者欲息疲癃殘疾顛連無告者欲遂
其生吾不能推父母之心安之懷之息之
遂之弗愛也愛其兄之子而不愛其鄰之
子非父母天下矣吾之親則愛之人之親
則不愛非父母天下矣愛於一家一家而
===
止耳非父母天下矣愛於一國一國而止
耳非父母天下矣父母愛子之心無所不
至無一不誠彼父兮生我母兮鞠我撫摩
鞠育無不遂其欲調護保養無不得其心
為君相者誠不以民視民而以吾子視民
不以民愛民而以愛子之誠愛民則天覆
地載之間日照月臨之下不必生於吾使
彼有怙凡天地之塞吾其體無一不得吾
愛之中不必鞠於吾使彼有恃凡天地之

translation_en:
…and ministers act as father and mother to all under Heaven: how, indeed, does this constitute the kingly Way? Consider the vastness of the realm and the multitude of its people. The hungry desire food; if I cannot extend a parent's heart to feed them, this is a failure to love. The cold desire clothing; if I cannot extend a parent's heart to clothe them, this is a failure to love. The old desire peace, the young desire care, the weary desire rest, and the infirm, disabled, and distressed who have no one to turn to desire to sustain their lives. If I cannot extend a parent's heart to give them peace, care, rest, and the means to sustain themselves, this is a failure to love. To love one's elder brother's children but not one's neighbor's children is not to act as father and mother to all under Heaven. To love one's own parents but not the parents of others is not to act as father and mother to all under Heaven. If love extends to one family and stops there, one is not acting as father and mother to all under Heaven. If love extends to one state and stops there, one is not acting as father and mother to all under Heaven.

The heart with which parents love their children reaches everywhere, and every expression of it is sincere. As the verse says, “Father, you begot me; mother, you nurtured me.” In caressing and rearing their children, they fulfill their every desire; in tending, protecting, and nourishing them, they satisfy their every wish. If rulers and ministers truly regard the people as their own children, and love them with the sincerity with which they love their children, then throughout all that Heaven covers and Earth bears, beneath the light of sun and moon, people need not have been begotten by me for me to give them paternal support. title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
帥吾其性無一不在吾愛之內視天下為
一家不隔藩籬而分比鄰視中國為一人
不梏形骸而分爾汝饑焉井田以食之寒
焉桑麻以衣之老焉不負戴以安之少焉
均其惠以懷之勞焉節其力以息之顛連
而無告者發政施仁以遂之慮性未復設
學校以教之慮訟未息明五刑以弼之非
徒見於言而必施諸事此心之誠也若秦
漢之少恩者無有焉非徒存諸中而必形
===
諸外此心之誠也若五伯之假名者無有焉
日出而作日入而息彼以為己力也而不
知所以出所以入者皆吾君相使之得
其所焉耕田而食鑿井而飲彼以為己功
也而不知所以食所以飲者皆吾君相使
之各遂其生焉不徒彼疆我里普天之下
皆覆吾王道蕩蕩平平之域不徒彼國我
家率土之濱皆樂吾王道熙熙皞皞之天
如是則天地之所以望宗子者始副宗子
punctuated: 帥吾其性，無一不在吾愛之內。視天下為一家，不隔藩籬而分比鄰；視中國為一人，不梏形骸而分爾汝。饑焉，井田以食之；寒焉，桑麻以衣之；老焉，不負戴以安之；少焉，均其惠以懷之；勞焉，節其力以息之；顛連而無告者，發政施仁以遂之。慮性未復，設學校以教之；慮訟未息，明五刑以弼之。非徒見於言而必施諸事，此心之誠也，若秦漢之少恩者無有焉；非徒存諸中而必形諸外，此心之誠也，若五伯之假名者無有焉。日出而作，日入而息，彼以為己力也，而不知所以出、所以入者，皆吾君相使之得其所焉。耕田而食，鑿井而飲，彼以為己功也，而不知所以食、所以飲者，皆吾君相使之各遂其生焉。不徒彼疆我里，普天之下皆覆吾王道蕩蕩平平之域；不徒彼國我家，率土之濱皆樂吾王道熙熙皞皞之天。如是，則天地之所以望宗子者始副，宗子
translation_en:
…what directs Heaven and Earth is my nature; not one lies outside my love. Regard all under Heaven as one family, without erecting fences to divide neighboring households; regard the Central Kingdom as one person, without being confined by bodily distinctions and separating one person from another. When people are hungry, feed them through the well-field system; when they are cold, clothe them through mulberry cultivation and hemp growing. When they are old, give them ease by sparing them loads on their backs or heads; when they are young, cherish them by distributing benefits equitably. When they toil, moderate the demands on their strength so that they may rest. For those in distress who have no one to appeal to, issue measures and practice benevolence so that their needs may be met. Concerned that their moral nature has not yet been restored, establish schools to instruct them; concerned that litigation has not yet ceased, clarify the Five Punishments to assist them. This must not merely appear in words but must be put into practice: such is the sincerity of this heart. There will be none of the scant kindness shown by the Qin and Han. It must not merely remain within but must manifest itself outwardly: such is the sincerity of this heart. There will be none of the appropriation of virtuous names practiced by the Five Hegemons.

They work at sunrise and rest at sunset, believing this to be the result of their own strength, unaware that their ability to go out and return rests entirely on our ruler and chief ministers enabling them to find their proper place. They plow fields for food and dig wells for drink, believing this to be their own achievement, unaware that their ability to eat and drink rests entirely on our ruler and chief ministers enabling each to sustain a full life. This extends beyond those boundaries and our settlements: all under Heaven are sheltered within the broad and even realm of our Kingly Way. It extends beyond those states and our households: all within the bounds of the earth delight in the harmonious and radiant world of our Kingly Way. title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
之所以任冢相之責者始得天下之所以
仰父母之願者始遂書曰元首明哉股肱
良哉此也易曰上下交而其志同者此也
非君相愛民之心一出於誠何以能成王
道之大若是乎稽之於古以堯舜之為君
而有皋陶稷契之為相當時萬邦協和黎
民於變四方風動萬國咸寧有此心此誠
也以禹湯文武之為君而有伊傅周召之
為相當時地平天成兆民允殖脩和有夏
===
四海永清有此心此誠也後世英君誼辟
政治或得或失人心或從或違非不能父
母天下也有此心無此誠故耳我
太宗文皇帝於萬幾之暇命儒臣集先賢格言
著為性理大全頒示天下於治道之篇有
取乎此其父母天下之心可以匹休先王
可以比隆前古可以垂教萬世者也愚何
幸佩服
聖訓謹論
punctuated:
之所以任冢相之責者始得，天下之所以仰父母之願者始遂。《書》曰：「元首明哉，股肱良哉！」此也。《易》曰：「上下交而其志同。」者，此也。非君相愛民之心一出於誠，何以能成王道之大若是乎？稽之於古，以堯舜之為君，而有皋陶稷契之為相，當時萬邦協和，黎民於變，四方風動，萬國咸寧，有此心此誠也。以禹湯文武之為君，而有伊傅周召之為相，當時地平天成，兆民允殖，脩和有夏，四海永清，有此心此誠也。後世英君誼辟，政治或得或失，人心或從或違，非不能父母天下也，有此心無此誠故耳。
我太宗文皇帝於萬幾之暇，命儒臣集先賢格言，著為《性理大全》，頒示天下。於治道之篇，有取乎此。其父母天下之心，可以匹休先王，可以比隆前古，可以垂教萬世者也。愚何幸佩服聖訓！謹論。
translation_en:
…only then is the purpose of entrusting responsibility to the chief councillor fulfilled, and only then is the wish of all under Heaven to look up to their rulers as parents satisfied. The Book of Documents says, “How enlightened the head! How worthy the limbs!” This is what it means. The Book of Changes says, “Those above and below communicate, and their purposes are one.” This, too, is what it means. Unless the ruler’s and his chief councillor’s love for the people proceeded wholly from sincerity, how could they achieve such greatness in the Kingly Way? Examining antiquity, when Yao and Shun were rulers, they had Gao Yao, Ji, and Xie as their chief councillors. In their time, the myriad states were brought into harmony, the common people were transformed, the four quarters were stirred as by the wind, and all states enjoyed peace. This was because they possessed this heart and this sincerity. When Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu were rulers, they had Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao as their chief councillors. In their time, the earth was brought to order and Heaven’s work completed; the multitudes truly flourished; the Xia realm was cultivated and harmonized; and all within the Four Seas enjoyed lasting tranquillity. This was because they possessed this heart and this sincerity. Among the outstanding rulers and righteous sovereigns of later ages, government sometimes succeeded and sometimes failed, and the people’s hearts sometimes followed them and sometimes turned away. It was not that they were incapable of acting as parents to all under Heaven. It was simply that they possessed this heart but lacked this sincerity.
Our Emperor Taizong Wen, in moments of respite from his myriad affairs, commanded his Confucian ministers to collect the exemplary sayings of former worthies and compile them into the Great Compendium of Human Nature and Principle (Xingli daquan), which he promulgated throughout the realm. In its section on the Way of Government, he included this teaching. His heart, intent on acting as a parent to all under Heaven, could rival the excellence of the former kings, equal the greatness of antiquity, and transmit instruction to ten thousand generations. How fortunate I, in my humble ignorance, am to embrace and observe these sagely instructions! Respectfully submitted as a discourse.

德鑒茲憲典之故事用飭

Though what they transmit is old, their institutions are renewed. I, a solitary man of humble station, have received this gift bestowed from the imperial palace. I have ample cause for gratitude, yet no means of repaying Your Majesty’s beneficence.

Your diligence and frugality match the spirit of Yu the Great; your generosity and benevolence surpass the virtue of Cheng Tang. You examine the precedents in these institutional statutes to adorn the cultural brilliance of this illustrious age. Compiling such a work was difficult, and transmitting it was no easy matter. text:

先聖後聖其揆一也夫豈有異乎哉粤自
伏羲繼天而王天不愛道龍馬負圖而出
于河其數自一至十因則之以畫八卦禹
治水功成地不愛寳神龜戴書而出于洛
其數自一至九因次之而叙九疇文王因
羲畫繫繇辭於是有先天後天之別武王
訪箕子陳洪範於是有先經後傳之分是數
聖人之書皆所以為天地立心為生民立
===
命為萬世開太平者也後世英君誼辟工
於詞章者若漢高帝之歌大風詠鴻鵠工
則工矣於治道乎何補勤於著述者若唐
太宗金鑑之書與帝範之作勤則勤矣於
躬行乎何有是豈可與前數聖人之書同
日而語哉洪惟
太祖高皇帝開國之初慮臣民染胡元之陋習
故頒大誥三編以訓廸之
太宗文皇帝臨御之日慮臣工失性分之正迺

列聖之書所以扶世導民者，亦此心也。孟子曰：「先聖後聖，其揆一也。」夫豈有異乎哉？粤自伏羲繼天而王，天不愛道，龍馬負圖而出于河，其數自一至十，因則之以畫八卦。禹治水功成，地不愛寳，神龜戴書而出于洛，其數自一至九，因次之而叙九疇。文王因羲畫繫繇辭，於是有先天後天之別；武王訪箕子，陳洪範，於是有先經後傳之分。是數聖人之書，皆所以為天地立心，為生民立命，為萬世開太平者也。後世英君誼辟，工於詞章者，若漢高帝之歌大風、詠鴻鵠，工則工矣，於治道乎何補？勤於著述者，若唐太宗金鑑之書與帝範之作，勤則勤矣，於躬行乎何有？是豈可與前數聖人之書同日而語哉？

…the writings of the successive sage emperors likewise sustain the world and guide the people through this same mind. Mencius said: “The earlier sages and the later sages follow the same standard.” How could there be any difference? When Fu Xi succeeded Heaven and became king, Heaven did not withhold the Way: a dragon-horse emerged from the Yellow River bearing a diagram, whose numbers ran from one to ten. Taking it as his pattern, he drew the Eight Trigrams. When Yu completed his work of controlling the floods, Earth did not withhold its treasure: a divine tortoise emerged from the Luo River bearing a writing, whose numbers ran from one to nine. Following their sequence, he set forth the Nine Categories. King Wen built upon Fu Xi’s drawings and appended divinatory statements; hence arose the distinction between the Prior Heaven and Later Heaven arrangements. King Wu consulted Jizi, who expounded the Great Plan; hence arose the distinction between the earlier canonical text and the later commentary. The writings of these several sages all served to establish a mind for Heaven and Earth, establish the destiny of the people, and inaugurate great peace for all ages. Among the brilliant rulers and righteous sovereigns of later times, those accomplished in literary composition included Emperor Gao of Han, who sang of the great wind and celebrated the swan. Accomplished he certainly was, but what did this contribute to the way of governing? Those diligent in authorship included Emperor Taizong of Tang, with his Golden Mirror and his Model for Emperors. Diligent he certainly was, but what did this amount to in personal practice? How could these writings be spoken of in the same breath as those of the several sages just mentioned?

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導左　批　〔策問性理難於條荅此篇剖析明白甚究心於理學者歟〕
考試官學正章　批　〔隨問隨荅不爲問目所窘可取〕
考試官教授鄭　批　〔策問理學正欲觀士子講貫之功而此篇敷陳明暢有學之士也〕
對善學者當窮夫不一之理尤當會夫至
一之理蓋不一者萬殊之分而至一者一
本之同也苟徒求不一之理於萬殊而不
===
能會其理於一本焉惡在其爲善學者哉
且自大舜命禹嗣位有人心道心之傳以
闢萬世心學之源而後之言心者皆本於
此自成湯誕告萬方有若有恒性之說以
發萬世性學之端而後之論性者皆原於
斯心之虛靈知覺一而已但生於形氣之
私者則爲人心原於性命之正者則爲道
心非有二心也寂然不動者太極之體感
而遂通者太極之用故曰心爲太極主宰
punctuated:
同考試官訓導左批〔策問性理，難於條荅。此篇剖析明白，甚究心於理學者歟？〕
考試官學正章批〔隨問隨荅，不爲問目所窘，可取。〕
考試官教授鄭批〔策問理學，正欲觀士子講貫之功，而此篇敷陳明暢，有學之士也。〕
對：善學者當窮夫不一之理，尤當會夫至一之理。蓋不一者，萬殊之分；而至一者，一本之同也。苟徒求不一之理於萬殊，而不能會其理於一本焉，惡在其爲善學者哉？且自大舜命禹嗣位，有人心道心之傳，以闢萬世心學之源，而後之言心者皆本於此。自成湯誕告萬方，有若有恒性之說，以發萬世性學之端，而後之論性者皆原於斯。心之虛靈知覺，一而已。但生於形氣之私者，則爲人心；原於性命之正者，則爲道心，非有二心也。寂然不動者，太極之體；感而遂通者，太極之用。故曰心爲太極主宰
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zuo, Assistant Instructor: 〔The policy question concerns human nature and principle, making it difficult to answer point by point. This essay analyzes the issues clearly. Surely its author has devoted considerable thought to the Learning of Principle?〕
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔He answers each question as it comes, without being constrained by the question’s headings. Worth accepting.〕
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Professor: 〔A policy question on the Learning of Principle is intended precisely to reveal a candidate’s achievement in studying and mastering it. This essay presents its arguments clearly and fluently: its author is a man of learning.〕
Response: Those who learn well should investigate principles in their multiplicity, and above all comprehend principle in its ultimate unity. Multiplicity consists in the distinctions among the myriad particulars; ultimate unity consists in their common foundation in a single root. If one merely seeks diverse principles among the myriad particulars but cannot comprehend their unity in a single root, in what sense can one be called a good learner?
When the great Shun commanded Yu to succeed to the throne, he transmitted the teaching of the human mind and the mind of the Way, opening the source of the learning of the mind for all ages. All subsequent discussions of the mind have been grounded in this. When Cheng Tang made his great proclamation to the myriad regions, he spoke of possessing a constant nature [?], initiating the learning of human nature for all ages. All subsequent discussions of human nature have derived from this.
The mind’s empty, numinous awareness is one and only one. Yet insofar as it arises from the particularity of bodily form and vital energy, it is the human mind; insofar as it originates in the rectitude of one’s nature and Heaven’s endowment, it is the mind of the Way. There are not two minds. Quiescent and unmoving, it is the substance of the Supreme Ultimate; responding to stimuli and thereby penetrating all things, it is the functioning of the Supreme Ultimate. Thus it is said that the mind is the governing master of the Supreme Ultimate…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
故集爲善陰隲孝順事實二書以勸諭之
宣宗章皇帝繼體守成集五倫書以化導天下
列聖之心卽羲禹文武之心
列聖之書卽羲禹文武之書然誥中善可爲法
如虞鐸之有德詹徽之執法非善之最者
乎惡可爲戒如鄭桓之貪汚蘇良之不才
非惡之最者乎陰隲中善之優者若鄧禹
仁恕是已孝順中孝之優者若虞舜大孝
是已五倫書如言文王爲人君止於仁爲
===
人臣止於敬爲人子止於孝爲人父止於
慈與國人交止於信豈非克盡五倫可以
爲萬世之法者乎噫
聖謨洋洋明如日星可以垂鑑戒于千古可以
明倫理于萬世愚也偏服
聖訓蓋有年矣茲因明問所及而述其管見如
此惟執事進教之幸甚
第三問
趙珝
punctuated:
故集《爲善陰隲》《孝順事實》二書以勸諭之。宣宗章皇帝繼體守成，集《五倫書》以化導天下。列聖之心卽羲、禹、文、武之心，列聖之書卽羲、禹、文、武之書。然誥中善可爲法，如虞鐸之有德、詹徽之執法，非善之最者乎？惡可爲戒，如鄭桓之貪汚、蘇良之不才，非惡之最者乎？《陰隲》中善之優者，若鄧禹仁恕是已；《孝順》中孝之優者，若虞舜大孝是已。《五倫書》如言文王爲人君止於仁，爲人臣止於敬，爲人子止於孝，爲人父止於慈，與國人交止於信，豈非克盡五倫，可以爲萬世之法者乎？噫！聖謨洋洋，明如日星，可以垂鑑戒于千古，可以明倫理于萬世。愚也偏服聖訓，蓋有年矣。茲因明問所及，而述其管見如此，惟執事進教之，幸甚！
第三問
趙珝
translation_en:
… Therefore, he compiled the two books Doing Good and Hidden Recompense (Weishan yinzhi) and True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi) to exhort and instruct the people. Emperor Xuanzong Zhang succeeded to the throne and preserved the achievements of his predecessors, compiling the Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun shu) to transform and guide all under Heaven. The minds of our sage emperors are the very minds of Fu Xi, Yu, King Wen, and King Wu; their books are the very books of Fu Xi, Yu, King Wen, and King Wu. In the Pronouncements, good deeds may serve as models: are not Yu Duo’s virtue and Zhan Hui’s enforcement of the law among the finest examples of goodness? Evil deeds may serve as warnings: are not Zheng Huan’s corruption and Su Liang’s incompetence among the worst examples of evil? In Hidden Recompense, Deng Yu’s benevolence and forbearance exemplify outstanding goodness; in Filial Obedience, Yu Shun’s great filial piety exemplifies outstanding filial conduct. The Book of the Five Relationships says, for example, that King Wen, as a ruler, rested in benevolence; as a subject, in reverence; as a son, in filial piety; as a father, in kindness; and in dealing with his countrymen, in trustworthiness. Does this not show complete fulfillment of the five relationships, providing a model for all generations?
Ah! The sage counsels are vast and abundant, bright as the sun and stars. They can transmit examples and warnings through the ages and illuminate ethical relationships for all generations. I, in my ignorance, have devotedly embraced [?] the sacred teachings for many years. Now, prompted by the matters raised in your discerning question, I have set forth my limited views in this manner. I would be most fortunate if you would offer me further instruction.
Third Policy Question
Zhao Xu

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
仁義禮智之性運用則惻隱羞惡恭敬是非
之情故曰心妙性情性之渾然至善一而
已以太極本然之全體言則為天命之性
以剛柔善惡之一偏言則為氣質之性非
有二性也孟子開悟人心之陷溺則曰性
無有不善猶水無有不下其有功於聖門
不既大矣乎荀子敢為大言而不顧則曰
人性惡其善者偽也其得罪於聖賢不既
多矣乎韓子性有三品之說可以言氣禀
===
之性若天命之性豈可以三品論乎六經
中言誠如云享於克誠之類是已言敬如
云克敬惟親之類是已雲峯胡氏嘗曰自
漢以來無人識誠字李邦直云不欺之謂
誠徐仲車云不息之謂誠程子云無妄之
謂誠言固善矣而義猶未盡惟朱子真實
無妄一言遂為不易之定論焉程子嘗曰
自秦以來無人識敬字既以整齊嚴肅言
之矣至其門人謝氏有所謂常惺惺法者
punctuated:
仁義禮智之性，運用則惻隱、羞惡、恭敬、是非之情，故曰：「心妙性情。」性之渾然至善，一而已。以太極本然之全體言，則為天命之性；以剛柔善惡之一偏言，則為氣質之性，非有二性也。孟子開悟人心之陷溺，則曰：「性無有不善，猶水無有不下。」其有功於聖門，不既大矣乎？荀子敢為大言而不顧，則曰：「人性惡，其善者偽也。」其得罪於聖賢，不既多矣乎？韓子性有三品之說，可以言氣禀之性；若天命之性，豈可以三品論乎？

六經中言誠，如云「享於克誠」之類是已；言敬，如云「克敬惟親」之類是已。雲峯胡氏嘗曰：「自漢以來，無人識誠字。」李邦直云：「不欺之謂誠。」徐仲車云：「不息之謂誠。」程子云：「無妄之謂誠。」言固善矣，而義猶未盡。惟朱子「真實無妄」一言，遂為不易之定論焉。程子嘗曰：「自秦以來，無人識敬字。」既以整齊嚴肅言之矣，至其門人謝氏，有所謂「常惺惺法」者
translation_en:
When the nature endowed with benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom comes into operation, it manifests as the feelings of compassion, shame and aversion, respect, and approval and disapproval. Hence the saying: “The mind wondrously unites nature and feelings.” Nature, in its undivided and utmost goodness, is one and nothing more. Viewed as the complete substance of the Supreme Ultimate as it originally is, it is called the nature conferred by Heaven; viewed in terms of partial endowments of firmness or softness, goodness or evil, it is called the nature of the psychophysical constitution. These are not two separate natures. To awaken human minds sunk in delusion, Mengzi said: “There is no human nature that is not good, just as there is no water that does not flow downward.” Was his contribution to the school of the sages not exceedingly great? Xunzi dared to make sweeping pronouncements without restraint, saying: “Human nature is evil; whatever is good in it is the product of deliberate effort.” Were his offenses against the sages and worthies not exceedingly numerous? Master Han’s theory that human nature has three grades may describe the nature arising from one’s endowment of vital energy. But how could the nature conferred by Heaven be discussed in terms of three grades?

In the Six Classics, sincerity is spoken of in such expressions as “Offerings are accepted through perfected sincerity”; reverence is spoken of in such expressions as “Those capable of reverence are drawn close.” Hu of Yunfeng once said: “Since the Han, no one has understood the word ‘sincerity.’” Li Bangzhi said: “Not deceiving is what is meant by sincerity.” Xu Zhongche said: “Never ceasing is what is meant by sincerity.” Master Cheng said: “Being without falsity is what is meant by sincerity.” These statements are certainly good, but they do not yet exhaust its meaning. Only Master Zhu’s phrase, “genuine and real, without falsity,” became the settled judgment that cannot be altered. Master Cheng once said: “Since the Qin, no one has understood the word ‘reverence.’” He had already described it in terms of orderliness, gravity, and solemnity; then his disciple Master Xie spoke of what he called the “method of constant wakefulness”…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
焉尹氏有所謂其心收斂不容一物者焉
言固當矣而旨猶未精惟朱子主一無適
一語遂爲至當之確論焉雖然人之一身
心爲之主人之一心敬爲之主性則此心
之理而誠則此心之實也真西山曰敬而
後能誠夫誠尚由敬而入況心也性也不
本於敬可乎故曰敬者一心之主宰萬事
之本根聖學所以成始而成終也愚雖不
敏請事斯語
===
第三問
高嶽
同考試官訓導李　批〔答問詳明蓋嘗用心於詩文者宜錄出之以式來學〕
同考試官教諭童　批〔策問歷代詩文士子多爲所窘惟此條陳無遺足見博洽之學〕
考試官學正章　批〔考據精切非直述問目者比〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔場中答策有如是卷〕
punctuated:
焉。尹氏有所謂其心收斂、不容一物者焉。言固當矣，而旨猶未精。惟朱子「主一無適」一語，遂爲至當之確論焉。雖然，人之一身，心爲之主；人之一心，敬爲之主。性則此心之理，而誠則此心之實也。真西山曰：「敬而後能誠。」夫誠尚由敬而入，況心也、性也，不本於敬可乎？故曰：「敬者，一心之主宰，萬事之本根，聖學所以成始而成終也。」愚雖不敏，請事斯語。

第三問
高嶽
同考試官訓導李批〔答問詳明，蓋嘗用心於詩文者，宜錄出之，以式來學。〕
同考試官教諭童批〔策問歷代詩文，士子多爲所窘。惟此條陳無遺，足見博洽之學。〕
考試官學正章批〔考據精切，非直述問目者比。〕
考試官教授鄭批〔場中答策有如是卷〕
translation_en:
… Master Yin spoke of gathering in the mind so that it admits not a single thing. These statements were certainly apt, yet their purport was still insufficiently refined. Only Master Zhu’s phrase, “concentrate on one thing without straying,” established a definitive account of perfect aptness. Nevertheless, the mind governs a person’s whole being, and reverent attentiveness governs the mind. Human nature is the principle of this mind, while sincerity is its actuality. Zhen Xishan said, “Only through reverent attentiveness can one attain sincerity.” If even sincerity must be approached through reverent attentiveness, how could the mind and human nature fail to be grounded in it? Thus it is said: “Reverent attentiveness governs the entire mind and is the root of all affairs. Through it, the learning of the sages is carried through from beginning to end.” Though I am slow of understanding, I ask to put these words into practice.

Third Question
Gao Yue 高嶽

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
者殊少此篇其最優者歟
吟詠性情而該物理者莫切於詩經緯天
地而宣教化者莫大於文蓋詩祖雅頌而
後可以爲治世之音文宗典謨而後可以
爲垂世之訓否則雖青錢萬選擲地金聲
尚可謂之詩文乎哉粵自夫子删述六經
之後而詩文衆體出焉由是詞人才子名
溢于縹囊染翰舒文卷盈於緗帙以文之
衆體言之諭以絲綸之語曰誥布以法度
===
之言曰制而誥則告也持而戒之者謂之
勑登而崇之者謂之冊而命猶令也攄臣
子之心於君后之前者曰表曰箋是也披
列事功而揭其行實者曰碑曰碣是也誄
者累其實行誌者識其名系若記非紀其
事乎序者緒而陳之傳者傳而信之若論
非言其倫乎别嫌疑而明之者辯也正是
非而著之者説也簡者質言之而畧也啓
者文言之而詳也狀者言之公上也檄者
punctuated:
者殊少，此篇其最優者歟？

吟詠性情而該物理者，莫切於詩；經緯天地而宣教化者，莫大於文。蓋詩祖雅頌，而後可以爲治世之音；文宗典謨，而後可以爲垂世之訓。否則，雖青錢萬選、擲地金聲，尚可謂之詩文乎哉？粵自夫子删述六經之後，而詩文衆體出焉。由是詞人才子，名溢于縹囊；染翰舒文，卷盈於緗帙。以文之衆體言之，諭以絲綸之語曰誥，布以法度之言曰制，而誥則告也。持而戒之者謂之勑，登而崇之者謂之冊，而命猶令也。攄臣子之心於君后之前者，曰表、曰箋是也。披列事功而揭其行實者，曰碑、曰碣是也。誄者，累其實行；誌者，識其名系。若記，非紀其事乎？序者，緒而陳之；傳者，傳而信之。若論，非言其倫乎？别嫌疑而明之者，辯也；正是非而著之者，説也。簡者，質言之而畧也；啓者，文言之而詳也。狀者，言之公上也；檄者，
translation_en:
…are exceedingly rare; might this piece be the finest among them?

For giving voice to human nature and feelings while encompassing the principles of things, nothing is more apt than poetry; for ordering Heaven and Earth and promulgating moral instruction, nothing is greater than prose. Only when poetry takes the Odes and Hymns as its ancestors can it become the sound of a well-governed age; only when prose takes the Canons and Counsels as its models can it become instruction handed down to later generations. Otherwise, even if a composition were like a bronze coin that passes ten thousand selections, or rang like metal when cast upon the ground, could it truly be called poetry or prose? After the Master edited and transmitted the Six Classics, the various forms of poetry and prose emerged. Thereupon, the names of literary talents filled books in pale-blue silk bags, and the volumes they wrote filled pale-yellow silk wrappers.

To speak of the various forms of prose: instruction conveyed in the silken language of imperial pronouncements is called a proclamation (gao); promulgation in the language of laws and standards is called a decree (zhi). Gao means to inform. That which restrains and admonishes is called an admonitory edict (chi); that which raises and honors is called an investiture patent (ce). A command (ming) is like an order. Those forms that unfold a subject’s heart before the sovereign are the memorial (biao) and the letter of presentation (jian). Those that set forth achievements and make known a person’s actual conduct are the stele inscription (bei) and the stone inscription (jie). A eulogy (lei) gathers together the deceased’s actual deeds; an epitaph (zhi) records the person’s name and lineage. As for a record (ji), does it not record events? A preface (xu) arranges and presents its subject; a biography (zhuan) transmits an account and establishes its credibility. As for a discourse (lun), does it not explain the principles of its subject? That which distinguishes doubtful matters and clarifies them is a disputation (bian); that which determines right and wrong and makes them evident is an explanation (shuo). A letter (jian) states things plainly and briefly; a formal communication (qi) states them in polished language and at length. A statement (zhuang) addresses the higher authorities; a proclamation (xi) is…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
激發人心也捷書不緘插羽而傳之者非
露布乎尺牘無封指事而陳之者非劄子
乎文體名目之義如此而曰解曰疏之類
可槩見矣以詩之衆體言之感傷時事托
於文辭謂之辭幽憂憤悱寓之比興謂之
騷而箴戒得失非箴乎程事較功考實訂
名謂之銘猗吁抑揚永言清濁謂之歌而
聲音委曲非曲乎高簡古淡者古也而側
非用上去入之聲乎法律精切者律也而
===
詠非其自咏嘆乎以直而言與衆而歌則
曰言曰謳感而發之憤而不怨則曰嘆曰
怨詩體命目之義如此而曰行曰引之類
可類推矣書變而為制為誥詩變而為騷
為賦傳志本春秋之遺體也序記即易與
記之遺體也以文論人如晁錯賢良策賈
誼過秦論班彪王命論揚雄作美新王莽
之記蘭亭皆膾炙人口者而東坡獨取孔
明之表豈非以其言辭激烈忠肝義膽讀
punctuated:
激發人心也。捷書不緘，插羽而傳之者，非露布乎？尺牘無封，指事而陳之者，非劄子乎？文體名目之義如此，而曰解、曰疏之類，可槩見矣。以詩之衆體言之，感傷時事，托於文辭，謂之辭；幽憂憤悱，寓之比興，謂之騷。而箴戒得失，非箴乎？程事較功，考實訂名，謂之銘；猗吁抑揚，永言清濁，謂之歌。而聲音委曲，非曲乎？高簡古淡者，古也；而側，非用上去入之聲乎？法律精切者，律也；而詠，非其自咏嘆乎？以直而言，與衆而歌，則曰言、曰謳；感而發之，憤而不怨，則曰嘆、曰怨。詩體命目之義如此，而曰行、曰引之類，可類推矣。
書變而為制、為誥，詩變而為騷、為賦。傳志，本春秋之遺體也；序記，即易與記之遺體也。以文論人，如晁錯賢良策、賈誼過秦論、班彪王命論、揚雄作美新、王莽之記蘭亭，皆膾炙人口者。而東坡獨取孔明之表，豈非以其言辭激烈，忠肝義膽，讀
translation_en:
…stirs people’s hearts. A victory dispatch sent unsealed, with a feather attached, is this not an open proclamation (lubu)? A short letter without a seal, setting out particular matters, is this not a memorandum (zhazi)? Such are the meanings of the names of prose genres; the categories called “explication” (jie), “exposition” (shu), and the like can be understood in broad outline from these examples. To speak of the many forms of poetry: being moved to sorrow by contemporary affairs and entrusting those feelings to literary expression is called ci, or lyric verse; lodging hidden grief and frustrated indignation in comparison and evocative imagery is called sao, or lament. And admonishing and warning concerning successes and failings—is this not an admonition (zhen)? Assessing deeds and comparing achievements, examining the facts and establishing their designation, is called an inscription (ming). Exclaiming in rising and falling cadences, prolonging words in clear and deep tones, is called a song (ge). And the winding inflections of sound—are these not a tune (qu)? What is lofty and spare, antique and unadorned, is ancient-style verse (gu); and oblique verse (ce) [?]—does it not employ the rising, departing, and entering tones? What is precise and exact in its formal rules is regulated verse (lü); and chanting (yong)—is this not giving voice to one’s own feelings in chant and sigh? Speaking directly and singing with a group are respectively called “utterance” (yan) and “singing” (ou); giving expression to emotion and feeling indignation without resentment are called “sighing” (tan) and “complaint” (yuan). Such are the meanings of the names of poetic forms; the categories called “ballad” (xing), “prelude” (yin), and the like can be inferred by analogy.
The Book of Documents developed into imperial decrees and proclamations; the Book of Odes developed into laments and rhapsodies. Biographies and records preserve forms inherited from the Spring and Autumn Annals; prefaces and accounts likewise preserve forms inherited from the Book of Changes and the Record of Rites. When judging people through their prose, examples such as Chao Cuo’s policy essay for the examination of the Worthy and Good, Jia Yi’s Discourse on the Faults of Qin, Ban Biao’s Discourse on the Royal Mandate, Yang Xiong’s Praise of the New Dynasty, and Wang Mang’s account of the Orchid Pavilion [?] are all widely admired and recited. title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
之令人生敬心乎以詩論人如蘇李之高
妙陳阮之冲淡曹劉之豪邁謝鮑之峻潔
徐庾之華麗皆有聲詩壇者而山谷獨取
子美之詩又非以其模寫風景忠君愛國
讀之令人生愛心乎我
國家
列聖繼作文運亨嘉光岳之氣完熙洽之運昌
崇經術以涵養天下之士氣重科目以收
拾宇宙之人才故上自臺閣下及衡門之
===
士莫不含英咀華發于詩文附翼於李杜
之鳳凰騰光于昌黎之山斗變化若雷霆
浩博若河漢誠足以鳴
國家之盛蓋與孔明二表子美諸詩同一機
軸也豈瑣瑣餘子著作所能彷彿其萬一
哉謹對
第四問
劉鎡
同考試官訓導陳　批　策問歷代人物名譽荅
punctuated:
之，令人生敬心乎？以詩論人，如蘇李之高妙、陳阮之冲淡、曹劉之豪邁、謝鮑之峻潔、徐庾之華麗，皆有聲詩壇者，而山谷獨取子美之詩，又非以其模寫風景、忠君愛國，讀之令人生愛心乎？我國家列聖繼作，文運亨嘉，光岳之氣完，熙洽之運昌。崇經術以涵養天下之士氣，重科目以收拾宇宙之人才。故上自臺閣，下及衡門之士，莫不含英咀華，發于詩文，附翼於李杜之鳳凰，騰光于昌黎之山斗，變化若雷霆，浩博若河漢，誠足以鳴國家之盛。蓋與孔明二表、子美諸詩同一機軸也，豈瑣瑣餘子著作所能彷彿其萬一哉？謹對。
第四問
劉鎡
同考試官訓導陳　批：策問歷代人物名譽，荅
translation_en:
…reading it inspires reverence, does it not? If we judge men through their poetry, there are the lofty subtlety of Su and Li, the serene simplicity of Chen and Ruan, the heroic sweep of Cao and Liu, the austere purity of Xie and Bao, and the ornate beauty of Xu and Yu—all renowned in the realm of poetry. Yet Shangu singled out the poems of Zimei. Was this not because their portrayal of scenery and their loyalty to the ruler and love of country inspire affection in the reader?
In our dynasty, sage sovereigns have succeeded one another, and literary culture has flourished. The vital force of the heavenly lights and sacred mountains is intact, and the age prospers in harmonious peace. Our rulers exalt classical learning to nurture the spirit of scholars throughout the realm, and esteem the examination system to gather talented men from all under heaven. Thus, from officials in the central government down to scholars dwelling behind humble gates, all savor the blossoms of literary excellence and express themselves in poetry and prose. They take wing with the phoenixes Li Bai and Du Fu and shine alongside Changli, a literary Mount Tai and Northern Dipper. Their transformations resemble thunder, their vast abundance the Milky Way. Their writings are indeed sufficient to proclaim our dynasty’s flourishing greatness. They spring from the same creative impulse as Kongming’s two memorials and Zimei’s poems. How could the writings of petty lesser men resemble even one ten-thousandth of their achievement? Respectfully submitted in reply.
Fourth Question
Liu Zi

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
者得一漏十此篇考據精詳篇末願以聖賢自負有
志之士也主司寧不為之刮目
同考試官訓導曾　批〔條答所問歷歷無遺該博之學於是乎見〕
同考試官教諭劉　批〔答問滔滔略無阻滯可嘉可取〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔敷對明白足見所學〕
考試官學正章　批〔策有考證宜居前列〕
三代以上人務實行不以名為尚三代以
===
下人少實行斯以名為尚君子於此可以
覘世道之升降矣請因明問所及而陳之
有一代之人物必有一代之名譽天下之
公論係焉不可誣也觀夫唐虞三代之時
大樸未散風俗醇厚教民以六德六行造
士以詩書禮樂當時人物名實相孚文德
攸濟誠有如執事之所言者自是以來士
有抱寸長挾片善者莫不著名當時而馳
譽後世如陳平相高祖而有名漢室韓安
punctuated:
者得一漏十。此篇考據精詳，篇末願以聖賢自負，有志之士也。主司寧不為之刮目？
同考試官訓導曾批〔條答所問，歷歷無遺，該博之學於是乎見。〕
同考試官教諭劉批〔答問滔滔，略無阻滯，可嘉可取。〕
考試官教授鄭批〔敷對明白，足見所學。〕
考試官學正章批〔策有考證，宜居前列。〕
三代以上，人務實行，不以名為尚；三代以下，人少實行，斯以名為尚。君子於此可以覘世道之升降矣。請因明問所及而陳之。
有一代之人物，必有一代之名譽，天下之公論係焉，不可誣也。觀夫唐虞三代之時，大樸未散，風俗醇厚，教民以六德六行，造士以詩書禮樂。當時人物，名實相孚，文德攸濟，誠有如執事之所言者。自是以來，士有抱寸長、挾片善者，莫不著名當時，而馳譽後世。如陳平相高祖而有名漢室，韓安
translation_en:
…those answering cover one point but omit ten. This essay’s examination of the evidence is precise and detailed. At its close, the writer expresses his resolve to hold himself to the standard of the sages and worthies: he is a man of ambition. How could the presiding examiners fail to regard him with new respect?
Associate Examiner Zeng, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔He answers the questions point by point, clearly and without omission. Here his extensive learning is revealed.〕
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔His answers flow freely, without the slightest impediment. Worthy of praise and acceptance.〕
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: 〔His exposition is clear and amply demonstrates his learning.〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔This policy essay is supported by examination of the evidence and deserves a place among the leading entries.〕
In the Three Dynasties and earlier, people devoted themselves to substantive conduct and did not prize reputation. After the Three Dynasties, substantive conduct became rare, and people consequently prized reputation. From this the gentleman can discern the rise and decline of the moral order. Allow me to set forth my views on the matters raised in your illuminating question.
Every age has its notable men, and necessarily has the reputations belonging to that age. These rest upon the impartial judgment of all under Heaven and cannot be falsified. Consider the time of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties: primordial simplicity had not yet dissipated, and customs were pure and generous. The people were taught the six virtues and six forms of conduct; scholars were trained through the Odes, Documents, rites, and music. Among the notable men of that time, reputation and substance confirmed one another, and achievements in civil virtue were realized, just as you have said. Since then, scholars possessing even a modest strength or a single good quality have invariably become renowned in their own time and had their reputations spread to later generations. For example, Chen Ping served Gaozu as chief minister and won renown in the Han imperial house, while Han An…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
國舉名士而多為國器此皆名之著于朝
廷者然也李膺稱鍾皓有至德可師謝安
處衡門有公輔之望此皆名之顯于天下
者然也以言其名揚于郡國者則有如名
聞梁楚之鄭當時進退以禮之雋不疑焉
以言其名播於外域者則有如威名流聞
匈奴之趙廣漢外夷願得為師之蕭穎士
焉不畏強禦有陳仲舉天下俊秀有王叔
茂焉此非名之形于誦詠者乎蘇李則蘇
===
味道李嶠其人也元白則元稹白居易其
人也此非名之見於並稱者乎諸葛亮關
羽張飛則謂之蜀三傑宗璟張說源乾曜
則謂之唐三傑竇武陳蕃之流號為三君
李膺荀昱之流號為八俊此其名之在於
票目者可見矣以馬威卿馬孺卿而謂之
鉅下二卿以王敬洪而謂之王山東以王
績而號為東皐子以白履忠而稱為梁丘
子此其名之係于地里者可知矣夫君子
punctuated: 國舉名士，而多為國器，此皆名之著于朝廷者然也。李膺稱鍾皓有至德可師，謝安處衡門有公輔之望，此皆名之顯于天下者然也。以言其名揚于郡國者，則有如名聞梁楚之鄭當時、進退以禮之雋不疑焉。以言其名播於外域者，則有如威名流聞匈奴之趙廣漢、外夷願得為師之蕭穎士焉。不畏強禦，有陳仲舉；天下俊秀，有王叔茂焉。此非名之形于誦詠者乎？蘇李，則蘇味道、李嶠其人也；元白，則元稹、白居易其人也。此非名之見於並稱者乎？諸葛亮、關羽、張飛，則謂之蜀三傑；宗璟、張說、源乾曜，則謂之唐三傑。竇武、陳蕃之流，號為三君；李膺、荀昱之流，號為八俊。此其名之在於票目者可見矣。以馬威卿、馬孺卿而謂之鉅下二卿，以王敬洪而謂之王山東，以王績而號為東皐子，以白履忠而稱為梁丘子，此其名之係于地里者可知矣。夫君子
translation_en:
…Han Anguo recommended eminent men, many of whom became pillars of the state. These are all examples of reputations established at court. Li Ying praised Zhong Hao as possessing consummate virtue worthy of emulation; Xie An, while living behind a humble gate, enjoyed the reputation of being fit for the highest ministerial office. These are examples of reputations renowned throughout the realm. As for those whose fame spread through the commanderies and kingdoms, there were Zheng Dangshi, whose name was known in Liang and Chu, and Jun Buyi, whose conduct accorded with ritual propriety. As for those whose fame spread to foreign regions, there were Zhao Guanghan, whose imposing reputation reached the Xiongnu, and Xiao Yingshi, whom foreign peoples wished to have as their teacher. For one who did not fear the powerful and overbearing, there was Chen Zhongju; for an outstanding talent of the realm, there was Wang Shumao. Are these not examples of reputations expressed in songs of praise?

“Su and Li” referred to Su Weidao and Li Jiao; “Yuan and Bai” referred to Yuan Zhen and Bai Juyi. Are these not examples of reputations manifested in paired names? Zhuge Liang, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei were called the Three Heroes of Shu; Zong Jing [?], Zhang Yue, and Yuan Qianyao were called the Three Heroes of Tang. Men such as Dou Wu and Chen Fan were styled the Three Gentlemen; men such as Li Ying and Xun Yu were styled the Eight Outstanding Men. Here we can see their reputations embodied in collective designations [?]. Ma Weiqing and Ma Ruqing were called the Two Qing of Juxia [?]; Wang Jinghong was called Wang of Shandong; Wang Ji was styled Master Donggao; and Bai Lüzhong was called Master Liangqiu. From these examples we can understand how their reputations were associated with geographical places. Now, as for the gentleman …

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
之學固貴于務實不徒以名為也然昌黎
有曰實大則聲宏亦理之自然也愚以為
前之諸人固可取以為法然必志伊尹之
志學顏子之學可也等而上之又當如孟
子願學孔子焉不然周子何以曰士希賢
賢希聖敢以是復明問
第五問
趙琮
同考試官訓導雷　批〔區處西事切中時宜其積學有素者乎〕
===
考試官學正章　批〔能言時務鑿鑿可行善於策者也〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔條陳時務而歸之得人灼然有見者宜冠兼場〕
試士而策以經世之務窮居而懷夫憂世
之心是皆為國為民而不徇乎一已之私
者也然明問彰彰敢默默乎且古者固能
授官歲計吏治令任賢去邪之法不異于
punctuated:
之學，固貴于務實，不徒以名為也。然昌黎有曰：「實大則聲宏。」亦理之自然也。愚以為前之諸人固可取以為法，然必志伊尹之志，學顏子之學可也。等而上之，又當如孟子願學孔子焉。不然，周子何以曰：「士希賢，賢希聖。」敢以是復明問。

第五問
趙琮
同考試官訓導雷　批〔區處西事切中時宜其積學有素者乎〕
考試官學正章　批〔能言時務鑿鑿可行善於策者也〕
考試官教授鄭　批〔條陳時務而歸之得人灼然有見者宜冠兼場〕

試士而策以經世之務，窮居而懷夫憂世之心，是皆為國為民而不徇乎一已之私者也。然明問彰彰，敢默默乎？且古者固能授官，歲計吏治，令任賢去邪之法不異于
translation_en:
…in his learning, the gentleman surely values practical substance and does not act merely for reputation. Yet Changli [Han Yu] said, “When substance is great, its resonance is far-reaching.” This too follows naturally from principle. In my humble view, the men mentioned above may certainly be taken as models, but one must aspire to Yi Yin’s aspirations and pursue Yan Zi’s learning. Advancing still higher, one should, like Meng Zi, wish to learn from Kong Zi. Otherwise, why did Zhou Zi say, “The scholar aspires to become a worthy; the worthy aspires to become a sage”? I venture to offer this in reply to your enlightened question.

Fifth Policy Question
Zhao Cong
Associate Examiner Lei, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔His handling of western affairs [?] precisely suits the needs of the times. Surely he has long cultivated his learning?〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔He can discuss current affairs, and his proposals are sound and practicable. He is skilled in writing policy essays.〕
Examiner Zheng, Professor, comments: 〔He sets out current affairs point by point and makes securing the right men the essential conclusion. His insight is clear; he deserves first place across both sessions [?].〕

To examine scholars by questioning them on the tasks of governing the world, and, while living in obscurity, to cherish concern for the world: both are acts undertaken for the state and the people, without yielding to personal self-interest. Your enlightened questions are so clear: dare I remain silent? Moreover, the ancients appointed men to office according to ability [?] and annually assessed officials’ administration. The present methods [?] of employing the worthy and removing the wicked do not differ from …

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
古然一有刺舉賢否不免混淆登用者未
必盡賢能之士被黜者未必皆貪婪之徒
不公甚矣要必重連坐之罰采輿論之公
而又得人與選如楊綰品裁清允則黜陟
自公矣何患乎賢否之混淆哉古者養民
以井田取稅以什一令足國裕民之計何
問乎古然一有調發公私未免困乏郎階
胥盜或竄于富室賣絲糶穀每苦於箭瘡
弊端多矣要必申義倉之制節浮冗之費
===
而又得人掌賦如劉晏經畫有方則用度
自足矣何憂乎公私之困乏哉守令隅之
帥帥所以承流而宣化也今
朝廷慮守令惟取胥監膺補之士則恐六事
或未脩也故近年來兼選進士出補外任
無非欲得其人以安黎庶而已然必益嚴
考課之法於六事脩舉者進之否則退之
如此則駟雖如魯恭卻虎如宋均者出矣
夫何至垂耳於鹽車乎將帥民之保障所
punctuated:
古。然一有刺舉，賢否不免混淆，登用者未必盡賢能之士，被黜者未必皆貪婪之徒，不公甚矣。要必重連坐之罰，采輿論之公，而又得人與選，如楊綰品裁清允，則黜陟自公矣，何患乎賢否之混淆哉？古者養民以井田，取稅以什一，令足國裕民之計，何問乎古？然一有調發，公私未免困乏，郎階胥盜或竄于富室，賣絲糶穀每苦於箭瘡，弊端多矣。要必申義倉之制，節浮冗之費，而又得人掌賦，如劉晏經畫有方，則用度自足矣，何憂乎公私之困乏哉？

守令，隅之帥帥，所以承流而宣化也。今朝廷慮守令惟取胥監膺補之士，則恐六事或未脩也，故近年來兼選進士出補外任，無非欲得其人以安黎庶而已。然必益嚴考課之法，於六事脩舉者進之，否則退之。如此則駟雖如魯恭、卻虎如宋均者出矣，夫何至垂耳於鹽車乎？將帥，民之保障，所
translation_en:
…the ancients. Yet whenever officials are investigated and impeached, the worthy and unworthy inevitably become confused: those appointed are not necessarily all worthy and capable men, and those dismissed are not necessarily all greedy men. This is profoundly unjust. It is essential to strengthen penalties imposing collective liability and heed impartial public opinion. Moreover, suitable men must participate in selection—men like Yang Wan, whose assessments were fair and judicious. Then dismissals and promotions will naturally be impartial. Why worry that the worthy and unworthy will be confused? In antiquity, the people were supported through the well-field system, and taxes were collected at one-tenth. How do present plans to provide adequately for the state and enrich the people differ from those of antiquity [?]? Yet whenever levies and requisitions arise, public and private resources alike inevitably suffer shortages. The garbled phrase “郎階胥盜” apparently concerns clerical theft and wealthy households [?]; those selling silk and grain repeatedly suffer from “arrow wounds” [?]. Abuses are numerous. It is essential to reaffirm the charitable granary system and curtail unnecessary expenditure. Moreover, suitable men must administer taxation—men like Liu Yan, whose fiscal planning was sound. Then resources will naturally suffice. Why worry about shortages in public and private resources?

Prefects and magistrates are the leaders of their localities [?], responsible for transmitting imperial influence and spreading moral instruction. The court now fears that, if prefects and magistrates are appointed solely from clerks and Imperial University students eligible to fill vacancies [?], the six duties may not be fulfilled. Thus, in recent years, it has also selected metropolitan graduates (jinshi) for appointments outside the capital. Its sole purpose is to obtain suitable men who will bring peace to the common people. Yet the procedures for evaluating performance must be made still stricter: those who fulfill the six duties should be promoted, and those who do not should be demoted. In this way, men like Lu Gong, associated here with the garbled phrase “駟雖” [?], and men like Song Jun, who drove tigers away, will emerge. Why should they end up like fine horses with ears drooping as they haul salt carts? Generals are the people's protective bulwark, the means by which…

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
使以身而運臂也今
朝廷慮將帥惟用膏粱紈綺之流則恐七德
或未諳也故邇年來請開武舉兼試文藝
無非欲得其人以衞疆埸而已然必益愼
簡閱之令於七德通曉者予之否則奪之
如是則凡販繒如樊噲屠狗如灌嬰者出
矣夫何患落魄於閭閻乎是則任賢去邪
也足國裕民也重守令也選將帥也四者
要必以得人爲本則政無不舉效無不臻
===
矣故曰爲政在人昔范希文自爲秀才時
便以天下之事爲己任厥後出爲世用在
朝爲名相在邊爲良將教人爲明師出守
爲循吏才氣老成先儒稱之心破膽寒西
陲詠之眞一代之豪傑也愚也他日倘得
效用於
明時肯使希文事業專美有宋也哉惟執事
進教之幸甚
punctuated:
使以身而運臂也。今朝廷慮將帥惟用膏粱紈綺之流，則恐七德或未諳也，故邇年來請開武舉，兼試文藝，無非欲得其人以衞疆埸而已。然必益愼簡閱之令，於七德通曉者予之，否則奪之。如是，則凡販繒如樊噲、屠狗如灌嬰者出矣，夫何患落魄於閭閻乎？是則任賢去邪也，足國裕民也，重守令也，選將帥也，四者要必以得人爲本，則政無不舉，效無不臻矣。故曰：「爲政在人。」
昔范希文自爲秀才時，便以天下之事爲己任。厥後出爲世用，在朝爲名相，在邊爲良將，教人爲明師，出守爲循吏。「才氣老成」，先儒稱之；「心破膽寒」，西陲詠之。眞一代之豪傑也！愚也他日倘得效用於明時，肯使希文事業專美有宋也哉？惟執事進教之，幸甚。
translation_en:
…so that the body may move its arms. Now the court, concerned that appointing commanders solely from among those raised on rich food and clothed in fine silks might leave the seven military virtues insufficiently understood, has in recent years called for military examinations that also test literary accomplishment. Its sole purpose is to obtain suitable men to defend the frontiers. Yet the rules governing selection and inspection must be administered with still greater care: those thoroughly versed in the seven virtues should receive appointments, and those who are not should be deprived of them. In this way, men such as the silk seller Fan Kuai and the dog butcher Guan Ying will emerge [?: the occupations assigned to these two men are reversed]. Why then worry that they will languish in obscurity among the common people? Appointing the worthy and removing the wicked, enriching the state and bringing prosperity to the people, attaching importance to prefects and county magistrates, and selecting commanders—these four undertakings must all rest fundamentally upon obtaining the right men. Then no measure of government will remain unimplemented, and no intended result will fail to be attained. Thus it is said: “The conduct of government depends upon men.”
In former times, Fan Xiwen, from his days as a student, took the affairs of the world as his own responsibility. Later, when he entered public service, he was a renowned chief councilor at court, an excellent general on the frontier, an enlightened teacher when instructing others, and a conscientious administrator when serving outside the capital. Earlier Confucian scholars praised his “talent, spirit, and seasoned judgment”; on the western frontier, songs told of “hearts shattered and courage chilled” by him. Truly he was an outstanding man of his age! If I, unworthy though I am, should one day have the opportunity to serve in this enlightened age, would I willingly allow Xiwen’s achievements to remain the exclusive glory of the Song? I would be most fortunate if you, honored sir, would offer me further instruction.

title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄後序
天生賢才所以輔相人主共
理天下者也人主誕膺天命
奄有四海必得賢才以資實
用相與贊襄治道黼黻皇猷
成一代之化垂萬年之統其
所關係不輕而重也審矣我
===
朝稽古爲治三年一大比網羅
賢才無非欲得實學之士以
資實用而已成化庚子山東
藩臬諸臣恪遵
成憲禮聘儒紳以司考較應試
之士千七百有奇時巡按泉
董學政者先試以汰其苐抑

山東鄉試錄後序

Postface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

Heaven produces worthy and talented men to assist the sovereign and join him in governing the realm. When the sovereign receives Heaven’s great mandate and possesses all within the Four Seas, he must obtain worthy and talented men for practical service. Together they advance good government and embellish imperial policies, bringing the civilizing work of an age to fruition and transmitting a succession lasting ten thousand years. What depends upon this is certainly weighty, not slight.

Our dynasty governs by examining antiquity and holds a great examination every three years to gather worthy and talented men. Its sole purpose is to obtain men of substantial learning for practical service. In the gengzi year of the Chenghua reign [1480], the officials of Shandong’s Provincial Administration Commission and Provincial Surveillance Commission scrupulously followed the established statutes and courteously invited learned gentlemen to conduct the examination and assessment. More than seventeen hundred men presented themselves for examination. title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
奔競杜僥倖革奸弊激昂士
氣凡貢院堂宇傾頽者新之
廢缺者舉之隘陋者擴而大
之其防範之周立法之嚴用
心之密視昔有加矣撤棘之
日得文之典實者七十五人
次第爲録異宜序於後夫山
東聖賢名邦士由科目出爲
===
世用爲
聖天子股肱心膂之臣後先相望
諸士子生長於斯涵被風教
非一日矣行將享有祿位攄
所藴竪所守施所養見之猷
爲措之政事上以堯舜其
punctuated: 奔競，杜僥倖，革奸弊，激昂士氣。凡貢院堂宇傾頽者新之，廢缺者舉之，隘陋者擴而大之。其防範之周，立法之嚴，用心之密，視昔有加矣。撤棘之日，得文之典實者七十五人，次第爲録，異宜序於後。夫山東，聖賢名邦，士由科目出爲世用，爲聖天子股肱心膂之臣，後先相望。諸士子生長於斯，涵被風教非一日矣。行將享有祿位，攄所藴，竪所守，施所養，見之猷爲，措之政事，上以堯舜其
translation_en:
…careerist scrambling, close off opportunities for undeserved success, eliminate fraud and abuses, and inspire the spirits of the scholars. All halls and buildings in the examination compound that were collapsing were renewed; those fallen into disuse or incomplete were restored; and those cramped and mean were enlarged. The thoroughness of the precautions, the strictness of the regulations, and the care devoted to these arrangements surpassed those of former times. When the thorn barriers were removed, seventy-five men whose compositions were grounded in the classics and substantial were selected. They were listed in order in a record, and Yi was to append a preface [?].

Shandong is a renowned land of sages and worthies. Scholars who have emerged through the examinations to serve the world, becoming the limbs and trusted inner counselors of the sagely Son of Heaven, have followed one another in succession. You scholars were born and raised here and have long been steeped in its moral influence and instruction. title: 成化十六年山東鄉試錄
text:
君下以堯舜其民斯無負乎素實
學科目實效聖賢之邦實有
其人爾不偉歟昔龍虎榜得
韓愈御科得陸贄天下後世
稱其得人非得人之多也人
有其實之謂也諸士子盡亦
思務其實俾後之稱科目得
===
人如今之稱昔也
直隸保定府安州儒學學正
績溪章英謹序
punctuated:
君，下以堯舜其民，斯無負乎素實學，科目實效，聖賢之邦實有其人爾，不偉歟？昔龍虎榜得韓愈，御科得陸贄，天下後世稱其得人，非得人之多也，人有其實之謂也。諸士子盡亦思務其實，俾後之稱科目得人，如今之稱昔也。
直隸保定府安州儒學學正，績溪章英謹序。
translation_en:
…their ruler into a Yao or Shun, and, below, transform their people into the people of Yao and Shun. Thus they will not betray their longstanding commitment to substantial learning [?]; the examination system will yield substantial results, and this land of sages and worthies will indeed possess men of true worth. Is this not magnificent? Formerly, the “dragon-and-tiger list” obtained Han Yu, and the imperial examination obtained Lu Zhi. Throughout the realm and in later generations, people praised these examinations for finding worthy men—not because they found many, but because those men possessed genuine substance. All you scholars should likewise strive for genuine substance, so that later generations may praise the examination system for finding worthy men just as we now praise the examinations of the past.
Respectfully composed as a preface by Zhang Ying of Jixi, Instructor in the Confucian School of Anzhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region (Zhili).
